title: A1 Darlington orange orbs
place: A1(M) north of Darlington, County Durham
summary: Ten orange orb-shaped lights were reported from the A1 north of Darlington. A local astronomer suggested such sightings are usually balloons or lanterns.

title: A470 faceless figure, Llyswen
summary: On 12 January 2008 a driver and passenger saw a tall man in a grey coat by the road with a featureless, faintly glowing oval head.

title: A55 flaming object over Llandudno
summary: A mechanic and three friends saw a low round object trailing flames pass over their car and disappear over the sea, and the coastguard took calls about bright lights offshore. A meteor was suggested but not confirmed.

title: A70 Harperrig abduction
place: A70 near Harperrig Reservoir, West Lothian
summary: Two men driving the A70 reported a two-tiered disc over the road that released a curtain of light, after which they found hours unaccounted for; under hypnosis they described an abduction. No explanation was given.

title: A75 Kinmount Straight
place: A75 Kinmount Straight, near Annan, Dumfries and Galloway
summary: In 1962 brothers Derek and Norman Ferguson reported a series of figures and animals that vanished as they drove at night, while their car rocked; other drivers reported phantom pedestrians in 1957, 1995 and 1997.

title: Aberconwy House prodding and moving plates
summary: Staff at the medieval merchant's house report being prodded in the loft, the smell of flowers, rattling and slamming doors, and display plates moving overnight. A woman by the loft fireplace and a Victorian man in the corridor are also described.

title: Abergele drifting lights
summary: A retired police officer reported fragmented white lights drifting over the town over several days, including one display lasting about ten minutes. No explanation was given.

title: Adelphi Hotel third floor
place: The Adelphi Hotel, Ranelagh Place, Liverpool
summary: Guests describe figures in naval dress, a figure hanging at a Crosby Room window and a ghost called George, with most reports from the third floor.

title: Aeron Valley carcass study finds felid bite marks
summary: Dr Ros Coard (University of Wales Trinity Saint David) examined sheep carcasses from the Aeron Valley in 2007. She concluded that bite marks on four of them were made by a medium-sized felid.

title: Afanc of Llyn Syfaddon
summary: The 15th-century poet Lewys Glyn Cothi placed the Afanc, a Welsh water monster, in Llyn Syfaddon. Other traditions link it to Llyn Barfog and a pool near Betws-y-Coed.

title: Altrincham dancing lights letter
summary: A child and father reported two small lights moving around each other, prompting a letter to the MoD. The ministry replied that it had no evidence of life beyond Earth and gave no explanation.

title: Am Fear Liath Mor, Ben Macdui
summary: Mountaineer J. Norman Collie said he fled the summit in 1891 after hearing giant crunching footsteps behind him in mist. Later climbers reported a looming figure; explanations include the Brocken spectre and fatigue.

title: Ancient Ram Inn
summary: Billed by its owners as the most haunted building in England with around twenty ghosts, it became a paranormal event venue after conversion to a guesthouse in 1968.

title: Anne Boleyn and Tower Green
place: Tower Green, Tower of London, London
summary: Anne Boleyn is said to lead a procession to the Chapel of St Peter ad Vincula; in 1864 a sentry bayoneted a white figure outside the King's House and was cleared after two witnesses backed him.

title: Apparition snapped at the old Crying Tree, Gateacre
place: Former Crying Tree, Grange Lane, Gateacre
summary: A Haunted St Helens investigator says a friend's photo on the staircase of the derelict mansion-pub caught a figure passing between the banisters. She insists no mark on the wall explains it.

title: Armadale Toblerone and stalled car
summary: A cable layer said his car stalled near a large Toblerone-shaped object. Police timings were found to conflict with his account.

title: Aughrim battlefield screams
summary: At the site of the 1691 battle, where Jacobite dead were left unburied, visitors report hearing screams.

title: Aveley abduction
summary: A family drove into a green mist and arrived home with about three hours missing.

title: Avenham Park coloured object
summary: A brightly coloured object hovering about 100 m up was reported in Preston, with a similar report from Wigan at about the same time. No explanation was given.

title: Aviator Tom Campbell Black at Speke airfield
summary: Record-breaking pilot Tom Campbell Black died in a runway accident at Speke in 1936, and his shadowy form is reported around the old hangars.

title: Ballygally Castle
place: Ballygally Castle, Coast Road, Ballygally, Co Antrim
summary: The castle hotel is reputed to be one of Ulster's most haunted places and keeps a 'Ghost Room'.

title: Balornock Poltergeist
summary: Knocking and flying furniture in a Glasgow home involved police, housing officials, clergy and investigator Archie Roy; it faded when a teenage boy at its centre left school.

title: Bangor hotel laser 'UFO'
summary: Four separate UFO reports were made over County Down. The official investigation traced the lights to lasers on the roof of a Bangor hotel.

title: Barguest of Trollers Gill
summary: A spectral black dog with huge eyes is said to haunt this limestone gorge; an 1830 ballad tells of a man found dead after trying to summon it.

title: Barnston silver humanoid
summary: A silver-suited humanoid was reported standing beside a craft at a road junction in the village. The claim was not verified.

title: Basement presence at Clifton Hall, Birkenhead
summary: Volunteers and staff at the 1840s Masonic hall describe shadows, noises and a feeling of being watched in the basement, and visitors hear furniture dragged upstairs. Ghost-hunt bookings now help fund the building and Most Haunted filmed there.

title: Bate Hall, Macclesfield
place: The Bate Hall, Chestergate, Macclesfield, Cheshire
summary: Staff report being touched and objects flying, with a boy called Billy and a grey lady said to be a woman hanged as a witch.

title: Bealings Bells
summary: From 2 February to 27 March 1834 the servants' bells rang violently with no one touching them, witnessed by Major Edward Moor FRS, his son and servants; no cause was found.

title: Beam of light burns woman at Denbigh Castle
summary: In spring 1964 a woman walking in the castle grounds found her dog cowering in a beam of light coming down from the sky. When she picked the dog up, her arm was burned and its fur was singed. Neither suffered lasting harm.

title: Beast of Bala shot, Llanuwchllyn
summary: A farmer shot an animal blamed for killing lambs; it turned out to be an escaped pet lemur.

title: Beast of Barnet lynx captured, Cricklewood
summary: Police and vets captured a young female Eurasian lynx after a chase across school playing fields. Named Lara, she went to London Zoo and later to a zoo in France.

title: Beast of Bennachie lambs and prints, Pitcaple
summary: The laird of Pitcaple Castle blamed a panther-like animal for partly eaten lambs near Whiteford, with large prints seen in snow, and a bailiff reported a long black cat at Pitcaple Bridge.

title: Beast of Bont sheep killings
summary: Twelve sheep were killed around Pontrhydfendigaid in June 1981, and government vets reportedly judged the killer stronger than a fox or dog. Further killings in the mid-1990s and around Ponterwyd in 2012 were blamed on the same 'beast'.

title: Beast of Brechfa migration claim
summary: A Ceredigion farmer whose ewes were killed said a police officer told him big cats winter in Brechfa Forest and summer in Myherin Forest near Devil's Bridge. Police disputed his account and no evidence was produced.

title: Beast of Buchan
summary: Twenty-two sightings of a big cat were logged in rural Buchan between May 2000 and January 2002, and local MP Alex Salmond raised livestock attacks in the House of Commons. No hard evidence was found.

title: Beast of Dartmoor puma release
summary: Decades of Dartmoor big cat sightings and livestock deaths were later linked to pumas reportedly released by animal trainer Mary Chipperfield when her Plymouth zoo closed in 1978.

title: Beast of Exmoor sheep losses
summary: A South Molton farmer claimed more than 100 sheep killed in three months, prompting a newspaper reward and a Royal Marines sniper deployment. No cat was found and the deaths are now attributed to large dogs.

title: Beast of Sydenham chases runner
summary: A man running at night with his dog said a five-to-six-foot cheetah-like animal stared at him and then chased them through the wood before giving up.

title: Beaumaris Gaol jailer and clock curse
summary: Visitors describe footsteps, cold spots, whistling and jangling keys attributed to a jailer, and dread in the execution room. Local lore says a man hanged in 1862 cursed the church clock so its faces never agree.

title: Beddgelert farmers' puma and paw casts
summary: A farming couple said they had seen a puma near their home, took plaster casts of paw prints and blamed big cats for livestock losses. The wife said the animal left her alone when she met it by the garden.

title: Belcher's Bar car stall
summary: A driver reported a flat disc passing over her car, dimming its lights and cutting out the engine and radio; an 11-year-old also saw it. No explanation was given.

title: Belfast Airport UFO investigation
summary: MoD papers released by the National Archives cover an investigation into a reported UFO near the airport. The released summary gives no explanation.

title: Belfast silent rising object
summary: A caller reported a silent object with flashing green and red lights rising from behind their house and flying towards the docks. No explanation was recorded.

title: Belvelly Castle mirrors
place: Belvelly Castle, near Cobh, Co Cork
summary: The tower house is said to be haunted by a faceless Lady Margaret Hardnett searching mirrors for her reflection and by a shipwrecked Spanish minstrel.

title: Bernie Brown on the Metropolitan Cathedral steps
summary: The 'pauper's ghost' is linked to the workhouse that once stood here; in one 1970s account a man met a stranger whose head flopped back on a broken neck. A medium said Bernie died falling from a workhouse window.

title: Berwyn Mountain incident
summary: A loud bang and tremor felt across North Wales, with lights seen on the mountain. Officially put down to an earthquake and poachers' lamps or meteors. Often called the 'Welsh Roswell'.

title: Bexleyheath hovering saucer
place: King Harold's Way, Bexleyheath, Greater London
summary: Around 30 people reported a saucer roughly 30 ft wide hovering over a residential street in daylight, with car engines said to have stalled. No explanation was recorded.

title: Big cat by Whitby Park tennis courts
summary: At about 8.30am a dog walker saw a slender, short-haired animal with a bushy tail, bigger than her spaniel, staring at her from six to eight feet away across a fence. It ran into bushes when her dog approached.

title: Big cat filmed after sheep killed, Askrigg
summary: A passer-by filmed a dark animal estimated at four to five feet long sitting in a field before it vanished behind a hill. A sheep had been found badly torn apart nearby.

title: Big cat on Old Colwyn golf course
summary: A man crossing the course at about 8pm saw a large black animal near one of the holes. He said he nearly passed out at the size of it.

title: Big cat roaming near Llanberis
summary: Police were told of a big cat, variously suggested as a puma or larger cat, roaming close to the village at the foot of Snowdon.

title: Black Beast of Ossett
summary: A black big cat nicknamed the Black Beast of Ossett was reported in the Coxley Valley in 2000.

title: Black Boy Inn nun, Caernarfon
place: Black Boy Inn, Northgate Street, Caernarfon, Gwynedd
summary: A nun is said to walk through the building, guests report a crying child that stops when spoken to, and a man has been seen in the bar.

title: Black cat and eviscerated ewe, Penuwch
summary: A smallholder reported seeing a large black cat twice within about two days, and one of her yearling ewes was found eviscerated.

title: Black cat filmed on lane, Pontybodkin
summary: A walker filmed a large black cat running across a lane in front of him. Weeks later a villager watched a dog-sized black cat sprint across a field near the same spot.

title: Black cat in Nercwys Forest above Mold
summary: At about 7.30am a dog walker saw a very large jet-black cat with a round head and pointed ears staring at her from about 50 yards away. It fled when her dog noticed it. Police later reported four sheep killed nearby that day.

title: Black cat near Cannock Chase Enterprise Centre
summary: Several workers saw a muscular black cat about three feet long pass close by in woodland at lunchtime; a police patrol searched without finding it.

title: Black cat stalking sheep, Holyhead
summary: A couple driving near the Premier Inn roundabout saw a large black cat stalking sheep; it slipped behind a bush and was gone when they looped back.

title: Black feline crosses Nercwys road junction
summary: A motorist driving at 45-50 mph after dark saw a large black cat-like animal dart across a junction.

title: Black lady and dog on Burton Marsh
place: Marsh between Burton and the Harp Inn, Neston
summary: A woman in black with a black dog was said to cross the Dee marsh at night, a tale perhaps spread by smugglers to keep people away.

title: Black leopard reported near Mold
summary: North Wales Police logged a report of a black leopard about 4 ft long in the Mold area. Officers investigated but saw nothing.

title: Black Monk of Pontefract
place: 30 East Drive, Chequerfield, Pontefract, West Yorkshire
summary: The Pritchard family reported a violent poltergeist nicknamed Fred that threw objects, made puddles and allegedly dragged their daughter up the stairs; the case was popularised by Colin Wilson in 1981.

title: Black panther in hedges, Llandudno
summary: A witness told police they had seen a black panther moving through hedgerows and insisted it was not a large dog. Officers found nothing.

title: Black panther near Brickfield Pond, Rhyl
summary: Several dog walkers saw a jet-black cat with pointed ears and a long tail bolt into a field near the nature reserve.

title: Black panther on rail line, Barkby, Prestatyn
summary: A morning walker reported a black panther with yellow eyes running along the railway tracks near Barkby Bridge.

title: Black panther running along road, Caernarfon
summary: A large black panther-type cat was reported running along a road. Officers visited the area but saw nothing.

title: Black puma stalking sheep at Glanwydden
summary: At dusk a man saw a large black cat creeping low through grass towards sheep behind the Queen's Head pub. He took two phone photos, but the animal had gone when he looked up.

title: Black Shuck at Bungay church
summary: During a violent storm a black dog was said to have run through St Mary's church, killing two worshippers. The same day it was reported at Blythburgh church, where scorch marks on the door are attributed to it.

title: Blackpool pier UFO report
summary: A UFO was reported above Blackpool pier and logged by the MoD UFO desk. No explanation was recorded.

title: Blairgowrie garden UFO and men in black
summary: A couple reported a UFO hovering over their garden and later visits from a group of men dressed in black. No explanation was given.

title: Blue Bell Hill hitchhiker
place: A229 Blue Bell Hill, near Aylesford, Kent
summary: Linked to a fatal crash in November 1965, drivers have reported a young woman who vanishes from their car or is hit and never found, including accounts from 1971 and 1972.

title: Blue light over Colwyn Bay and Llandudno
summary: A brilliant blue light crossed Wales and was seen from the south up to Anglesey. A Rhos Point fisherman said it lit the whole sky over Colwyn Bay and Llandudno for several seconds. The RAF said it was not an aircraft, and a meteor was suggested.

title: Bodelwyddan Castle Blue Lady
summary: A lady in a blue dress is said to walk the sculpture gallery and pass through a wall, and children are heard playing in the toy room. A security guard reported seeing only a pair of legs in buckled shoes and white stockings.

title: Beast of Bodmin Moor
summary: Repeated sightings of a large black cat and livestock kills. A 1995 government study found no proof.

title: Bold Street time slips
summary: Several people report stepping briefly into a 1950s or earlier version of the street.

title: Bonneted lady on Woodchurch Road
summary: An older woman in black with a bonnet appeared on the road and suddenly vanished; a newspaper said cyclists braked hard to avoid her. Others saw a small ball of fire that quickly disappeared.

title: Bonnybridge sightings
summary: Area with thousands of reported sightings since the early 1990s, dubbed the Falkirk Triangle.

title: Bonsall pink object filmed
summary: A resident filmed a luminous pink object for several minutes and other villagers reported lights. No explanation was given.

title: Borley Rectory
summary: Once called the most haunted house in England. A nun, a phantom coach and wall writings were reported. The rectory burned down in 1939.

title: Bow wave crossing Loch Arkaig
summary: Campers at the west end of the loch watched an object about the bulk of a small cow cross the bay at 4am, leaving a large bow wave.

title: Bownessie photographs, Windermere
summary: Anomalous photographs of a humped shape in Windermere in 2011 led to the nickname Bownessie. Sceptics noted similar images have turned out to be floating debris.

title: Boy scratched by 'big cat', Trellech
summary: An 11-year-old searching for his lost cat was left with claw marks on his cheek and police issued a big cat warning. A police helicopter search found nothing.

title: Braddan silvery-blue dart
summary: A silvery-blue dart or sphere was photographed over Braddan in daylight, and an off-duty police officer said they saw something at the same time. No explanation was given.

title: Bramham Park phantom horses
place: Bramham Park, Bramham, Leeds, West Yorkshire
summary: Phantom war horses and hoofbeats are reported in the park and linked locally to the Battle of Bramham Moor in 1408.

title: Brentford Griffin
summary: A local man reported a winged, dog-like creature over Braemar Road in summer 1984 and again in 1985, and others described a large black bird-like shape on the gasometer. Much of the testimony is now regarded as hoax or media-driven.

title: Bright light and flash over Wrexham
summary: Around 7am, people in Wrexham, Brymbo, Rhos, Garden Village and Minera reported a bright light moving across the sky, then a bright flash about a minute later. No cause was confirmed.

title: Britannia Inn monks, Horseshoe Pass
place: Britannia Inn, Horseshoe Pass, Llangollen, Denbighshire
summary: Phantom monks are said to inhabit the inn, with monk-like shadows seen in the public rooms.

title: Brixham domed object
summary: A dome-shaped object with an apparent door was watched hovering for about an hour and was logged by the Berry Head coastguard. No explanation was given.

title: Broad Haven school sighting
summary: Around 14 boys and one girl aged 9-11 reported a silvery, domed cigar- or saucer-shaped craft in a boggy field roughly 300-400 yards from the school at lunchtime, some describing a silver-suited figure with pointed ears beside it. Headteacher Ralph Llewellyn had the pupils draw it separately and the drawings were strikingly similar; investigators found no traces in the muddy ground. Existing entry - extra sources added (OSM places the school building at 51.7783,-5.0999).

title: Broad Haven school: second sighting by David Davies
place: Broad Haven C.P. School, Broad Haven, Pembrokeshire
summary: Pupil David Davies, who had stayed indoors at lunch, reported seeing a silver cigar-shaped object slightly longer than a coach rise from behind a hedge and trees later the same day. Several other boys said the object appeared to be stuck and tugging at a silver object. Davies retold the account as an adult in Netflix's Encounters (2023).

title: Broad Haven school: teacher and dinner ladies' sighting
place: Broad Haven C.P. School, Broad Haven, Pembrokeshire
summary: Teacher Mrs Morgan reported a large shining ridged oval object, and said a small whirlwind of dust crossed the playground as it rose; two canteen ladies said they saw an object on the ground, a figure climbing into it and the craft rising up a slope. Some accounts date the staff sighting to 17 February 1977, others to mid-April. The staff at first assumed it was a sewage tanker.

title: Broken-neck man in the Epstein Theatre
summary: A pale man with his head lolling on his shoulder has been seen in the dressing rooms since the 1920s and is said to herald misfortune. In February 1993 a staging of The Devil Rides Out was reportedly plagued by disturbances after a pentagram was chalked on stage.

title: Brown-habited figure on the A5123 at Halkyn
summary: In the early 1970s two men in a car saw a figure in a brown habit step out in front of them, and the driver braked hard, but nothing was found. Readers linked it to a monk-like ghost near Holywell and a misty figure on Halkyn Mountain.

title: Brown Lady of Raynham Hall
summary: Sightings date from 1835, and on 19 September 1936 Country Life photographers captured a veiled figure on the staircase; sceptics suggest double exposure.

title: Bull Hotel monk, Abergele
place: The Bull, Chapel Street, Abergele, Conwy
summary: Staff and guests report a monk said to have died in a fall and a young motorcyclist killed nearby, along with shadows, cold spots and a woman's figure.

title: Burnley silver cigar
summary: A taxi driver and passenger watched a silent silver cigar with a pulsing light hover, change shape and move back and forth for about three minutes. No explanation was given.

title: Bus driver's vanishing monk, Walton
summary: Driving to work at 3.45am, a bus driver watched a monk cross in front of his car and vanish; he later heard the area was said to be haunted by a monk and nun.

title: Caernarfon green object
summary: A witness reported a green, star-like object with red on one side that looked as if it would hit their house. It was logged in MoD files without explanation.

title: Calvine photograph
summary: Photo of a large diamond-shaped object hovering above the hills with a jet nearby. The image was released in full in 2022.

title: Caracal shot by police, Fintona
summary: Police shot a loose wild cat, reported as a caracal though a police report called it a lynx.

title: Carlisle silver cone
summary: Two teachers watched a silent silver cone-shaped object about 100 m up for around five minutes before it vanished. A local monitor speculated about a spy plane.

title: Carrickmacross retracing object
summary: A slow-moving object was watched for about half an hour travelling east to west and repeatedly retracing its path; witnesses ruled out an aircraft. No explanation was given.

title: Castle Hotel chambermaid, Conwy
summary: The hotel is said to be haunted by an angry chambermaid whose last wish was ignored, and guests report a phantom cat climbing onto beds at night.

title: Castle Mona green lady
place: Castle Mona, Douglas, Isle of Man
summary: Reports include a lady in green near the Dickens Bar and twin girls seen at the foot of beds.

title: Castle Rushen White Lady
place: Castle Rushen, Castletown, Isle of Man
summary: The 14th-century castle, scene of many executions, has reports of shadowy figures, a White Lady and a Woman in Black.

title: Castlemartin dunes metallic object and 'ray' men
summary: A Mr Thomas reportedly found a metallic object in the dunes and was warned off with 'powerful rays' by two men who said they had visited Earth for centuries. The date was not recorded beyond 1952; coordinates are for Castlemartin village.

title: Cat-like beast attacks foal at Felingwm
summary: In 1997 a 'cat-like beast' was reported to have attacked a foal at Felingwm, near Carmarthen.

title: Catherine Howard, Hampton Court
place: Haunted Gallery, Hampton Court Palace, London
summary: Legend says Catherine Howard broke from her guards in 1541 and ran along the gallery to plead with Henry VIII; it has since been called the Haunted Gallery.

title: Childwall man whose family never existed
summary: After a crash at Fiveways while rushing his pregnant wife to hospital, a man woke to be told his wife and three children had never existed. Tom Slemen calls it one of his strangest cases; names were changed.

title: Chirk Castle cave of no return
summary: Legend tells of a cave near the castle entrance that draws in anyone who comes within five paces. A fiddler who walked in playing one Halloween never came out, and a fox fled out smelling of brimstone.

title: Churche's Mansion, Nantwich
place: Churche's Mansion, Hospital Street, Nantwich, Cheshire
summary: Three ghosts, including a Civil War cavalier and the original owner's father, are said to haunt the 16th-century house, where objects move; it was investigated in 2007.

title: Circular object and light over Llyn Tegid
summary: Two brothers visiting family saw a circular object heading towards the Berwyns, then a brighter, oddly flashing light over the far side of the lake that climbed quickly. A Llanuwchllyn family reported orange circular objects over the mountains.

title: Cleethorpes glass sphere tracked by RAF Manby
summary: A large glassy sphere was watched over the coast for more than an hour and reportedly painted on radar at RAF Manby, departing as RAF aircraft approached. No explanation was given.

title: Clifden oval orbs photographed
summary: Two oval orbs were seen and photographed; conventional aircraft were said to have been ruled out. No identification was offered.

title: Clwydian Range UFO flap
summary: The Welsh Federation of Independent Ufologists recorded a cluster of UFO reports around the Clwydian Range, Prestatyn, Meliden and Dyserth in 1985 and 1986.

title: Coal-cellar boy of Calderstones House
summary: A Victorian boy crushed by a coal delivery is said to haunt the mansion; staff describe sickness after taunting him and footsteps along a corridor at night. The cellar is now sealed.

title: Coal-throwing outbreak, Myers Street
summary: Windows along the street were smashed by flying lumps of coal, and the breakages carried on even after police began patrolling.

title: Combermere Abbey ghost photo
summary: A long-exposure photograph of the library taken in 1891, while Lord Combermere's funeral was under way, appears to show a figure in his chair.

title: Cononley police domed craft
summary: Two police officers reported a domed object about 100 ft across with lit portholes near the A629. No explanation was recorded.

title: Coombs children: three UFOs, a ladder and a red box
place: Clifftop fields near Ripperston Farm, Pembrokeshire
summary: Coombs children (named as Keiran and Layanne in one account) reported three hovering UFOs, the lowest of which lowered a metal ladder down which a silver-clad figure climbed, leaving a bright red 'box' that could not afterwards be found. The children reportedly developed blotchy red patches on their skin the next day. Coordinates approximate (clifftop fields seaward of the farm).

title: Coombs twins see a figure walk through a fence
place: Clifftop fields near Ripperston Farm, Pembrokeshire
summary: Twin daughters Layann and Joann Coombs reported a silver, faceless, square-headed figure that walked through a hedge and a barbed-wire fence and passed within about 12 ft of them. The family later reported large footprints.

title: Corbridge giant arrowhead
summary: A huge arrowhead-shaped object, described as the size of ten football pitches, was reported. A local astronomer argued such sightings can usually be explained, but none was given for this case.

title: Corpse candle sinks into Silian churchyard
summary: Owen Evans of Maesydderwen, Llansawel, told Ceredig Davies that in his boyhood a young man saw a light inside the locked Silian church. With Evans's father he watched it move and sink into the ground, and they marked the spot with a stick. A death followed and the person was buried on that spot.

title: Corpse candles of Bloody Acre, Childwall
place: Bloody Acre, All Saints Church, Childwall
summary: A patch of scrub next to Liverpool's oldest church is said to be protected by an old promise never to build on it. Tales describe coloured orbs ('corpse candles'), 'black goblins' and a dark figure that rises before wars.

title: Cosford incident
summary: A large triangular craft reported over RAF Cosford and RAF Shawbury. Investigated by the MoD's Nick Pope.

title: Craigluscar Reservoir metallic disc
summary: An angler photographed a humming metallic disc hovering over the reservoir for more than 15 minutes before it sped off. Checks with the RAF, airports and police found no known traffic.

title: Cranwell 'possible missile'
summary: An RAF pilot and student flying at 2,000 ft reported an object climbing to around 25,000 ft before appearing to explode. RAF and civil police investigated; no explanation was given.

title: Crewe Lyceum Theatre
place: Lyceum Theatre, Heath Street, Crewe, Cheshire
summary: Reported ghosts include a lady in white said to be a ballerina, a stagehand, a hooded figure and a lost child; an exorcism was reportedly held in 1969.

title: Croxteth Hall CCTV figure
summary: In April 2009 a CCTV clip appeared to show a glowing figure moving along a path towards the hall before vanishing, and the council brought in ghost specialists. Earls of Sefton are traditionally said to walk the grounds.

title: Crumlin ringed-light object
summary: A caller told police they had seen an object with eight to ten lights around its edge. No explanation was recorded.

title: Crying princes at Farndon Bridge
summary: Two young princes, legend says, were thrown from the bridge by Roger Mortimer, and their cries are heard on stormy nights.

title: Culloden battlefield
summary: Phantom soldiers and the sounds of battle are said to occur around the 16 April anniversary, and a visitor in 1936 reportedly saw a dead Highlander by a grave mound.

title: Cwm Mountain charcoal triangle
summary: A Llandudno couple reported a charcoal-coloured triangular craft over Cwm Mountain, and the following month an egg-shaped object with a sphere suspended beneath it. No explanation was given.

title: Cwys yr Ychain Bannog: furrow left by dragging a giant reptile
place: ridge c. 3 miles from Tregaron, Ceredigion
summary: A ridge about three miles from Tregaron is called 'Cwys yr Ychain Bannog'. Tradition says it was made when two Bannog oxen dragged away the carcass of a huge reptile killed by local people in ancient times. Location is approximate.

title: Cyril John's swinging egg and suspended silver figure, Milford Haven
summary: Cyril John, 64, reported an orange-lit egg-shaped object about 4 ft long swinging in a 50-60 ft arc, with a silver-suited figure hanging about 40 ft up, for roughly 25 minutes. It is one of several silver-suited figure reports from the spring 1977 wave.

title: Dairy driver sees large black cat at Ffairfach
summary: The day after the Llangadog creamery sighting, a dairy driver reported a large black cat at the edge of woodland at Ffairfach, about ten miles from Llangadog.

title: Dark disc photographed over Bidston Hill
summary: Engineer Mike Dunne, 25, photographed a dark disc-shaped object hovering over houses near Bidston Hill before it vanished; dozens of others were said to have seen it. Slemen calls the hill a UFO 'window area'.

title: Dark object filmed over Caernarfon Castle
summary: A local man filmed 40 seconds of daylight video showing a small dark object hovering over the castle. It then sank slowly and disappeared behind the walls.

title: Dark shape over Cardigan Bay from Llanrhystud
place: Morfa Farm caravan park, Llanrhystud, Ceredigion
summary: Katie Moore, 29, and four friends reported an unlit dark shape in the sunset sky over Cardigan Bay at 10:40pm that vanished while being photographed, briefly reappeared and vanished again.

title: Daylight phantom funeral at Llanbadarn Odwyn
place: Llanbadarn Odwyn churchyard, near Llangeitho, Ceredigion
summary: Harvest workers near Llangeitho reportedly saw a 'toili' (phantom funeral) at midday in Llanbadarn Odwyn churchyard. A real funeral followed soon afterwards.

title: Debbie Swan's football-sized UFO, Herbrandston
summary: Thirteen-year-old Deborah (Debbie) Swan reported a silver, football-shaped object moving erratically by a hedgerow on the same day as Mark Marston's encounter.

title: Robert Taylor, Dechmont Woods
summary: A forestry worker said spiked spheres grabbed him beside a hovering dome. Police recorded it as an assault; ground marks were found.

title: Deer carcasses at Woodchester Park
summary: Two roe deer carcasses with injuries some experts said matched a big cat kill were sampled by Warwick University. DNA tests found only fox and deer.

title: Devon 'flying cross' police chase
summary: Two police constables followed a bright cross-shaped light by car for around 15 minutes and reported a second object joining it. The sighting was attributed to Venus.

title: Diamond-shaped craft over Valle Crucis Abbey
summary: A Colwyn Bay couple camping at the abbey said a huge, silent diamond-shaped object hovered roughly 60 feet up. They described spotlights that lit the ruins like a stadium and red lights arranged in a cross.

title: Dog killed, huge black cat and smaller cat seen near Llangadog
summary: A home help found a neighbour's dog, Peter, killed on a farm near Llangadog. He said he saw a huge black cat with a smaller cat, and police saw one silhouette running away.

title: Dome-shaped light on the Broad Haven to Milford Haven road
place: Road between Broad Haven and Milford Haven, Pembrokeshire
summary: Dorothy Cale, her 10-year-old son Daniel, Yvonne Andrews and Anne Berry reported a dome-shaped light about 5-6 ft across flashing four times above a hedge. It is cited as one of the earliest reports of the 1976-77 St Brides Bay wave. Location approximate (midpoint of the route).

title: Double of a living man seen ploughing field, Gogoyan
summary: A servant ploughing at Gogoyan saw his master, John Evans, walking near him in the field one afternoon. Evans had been in Aberystwyth, over twenty miles away, all day and said the servant had seen 'only my spirit'. Ceredig Davies records this as a family story about his own grandfather.

title: Douglas Bay fireball
summary: A fireball was reported travelling across Douglas Bay at night. No explanation was given in the report.

title: Dr John Harries, the wizard of Cwrtycadno
summary: John Harries (d. 1839), physician, astrologer and 'dyn hysbys', reportedly told searchers where a murdered girl was buried under a tree with a bees' nest. He was then brought before the Llandovery magistrates and discharged. He was said to keep a chained, padlocked book of spells that he opened only once a year.

title: Duckett's Grove
summary: Visitors report whispers, apparitions, organ music, a phantom carriage and servants' voices in the kitchens.

title: Dudley 'Dorito' triangles
summary: A series of silent black triangle sightings over the Black Country between 2007 and 2011 earned the nickname 'Dudley Dorito'. No explanation was established.

title: Dunkenhalgh governess Lucette
summary: Lucette, a governess said to have drowned herself after being deceived by an officer, is reported in a winding sheet, especially on Christmas Eve.

title: East Glasgow three white objects
summary: Three white objects were reported over the east of the city. Russian Antonov An-30 survey aircraft were put forward as the likely cause.

title: East Hull slow lights
summary: Residents watched slow-moving lights for about an hour late in the evening. They were attributed to the Northern Lights.

title: East Lancs Road roadside aliens
summary: A motorcyclist heading for Manchester in the early hours claimed two beings in ski-suit-like outfits stopped and spoke to him. No corroboration was recorded.

title: Edinburgh Vaults voices
summary: During a 2009 BBC overnight filming, a microphone recorded about 20 minutes of unexplained voices that the presenter did not hear; no source was identified.

title: Egryn lights and the Mary Jones revival
summary: During the 1904-05 Welsh revival, preacher Mary Jones and many others reported balls and columns of light around Egryn Chapel and along the Dyffryn-Llanbedr road. Journalists from the Daily Mail, Daily Mirror and Daily News came to investigate, and a local police constable also reported a light he could not explain. Proposed causes include earth lights on the Mochras Fault, marsh gas and gorse fires.

title: Eleven orange lights over the Menai Strait
summary: During a Faenol Festival evening, a Llanfairpwll family and festival-goers watched 11 silent orange lights in small groups travel up the Strait, stop at the Britannia Bridge, turn towards Bangor and climb steeply away. The fireworks had not started yet, and the RAF reported no aircraft.

title: Elizabeth Warburton of Stanley Palace
summary: Former owner Elizabeth Warburton is seen walking through walls, alongside a Tudor-dressed man, a WWII officer and a grey-haired woman by the piano. Visitors report banging, crying children and footsteps.

title: Emley Moor mast police sighting
summary: West Yorkshire Police logged a possible UFO after officers and other witnesses watched a static cylindrical object with a white light at each end near the TV mast for several minutes. The CAA could not identify it as an aircraft.

title: Enfield poltergeist
summary: Furniture moving, knocking and a gruff voice reported in a council house, investigated by the Society for Psychical Research.

title: Exercise Mainbrace disc over RAF Topcliffe
summary: During the NATO Exercise Mainbrace a silver disc was reported following a Meteor jet back towards RAF Topcliffe, and RAF aircraft later chased a sphere over the North Sea. The case was raised in Parliament; no explanation was given.

title: Explosion and white light over Rhuddlan
summary: A police officer reported a large explosion accompanied by an intense white light over the town.

title: Family sees flashing lights moving fast above car, A40 Tal-y-llyn
place: A40 towards Tal-y-llyn, near Brecon, Powys
summary: Around 5:30pm Richard Davis, his wife and two children were driving home from Brecon when the youngest son saw flashing lights moving at speed in the sky above the car. The family called it 'unnerving'.

title: Farm servant spends a year and a day with the fairies, Allt Ddu
place: Allt Ddu farm, between Pontrhydfendigaid and Tregaron (Cors Caron), Ceredigion
summary: A servant went missing near the Gors Goch bog and his fellow servant was tried for murder and acquitted. On a conjurer's advice, the family went to a set spot a year and a day later and found him dancing in a fairy ring. Pulled out, he believed only minutes had passed. The story was first published in 'Cymru' (May 1893) by D. Lledrod Davies.

title: Farrier ghost at the Trevor Arms, Marford
place: Trevor Arms, Marford Hill, Marford, Wrexham
summary: Reported spirits at the former coach house include a Cavalier, a young girl and a Victorian farrier in a leather apron. When a resident told the farrier to leave, he is said to have answered back and vanished. Guests also report drawers opening by themselves.

title: Father and son of Leasowe Castle
summary: Legend says a man and his son were imprisoned here and the father killed the boy and then himself rather than starve; the pair are said to appear in the room where they died. The castle is now a hotel.

title: Fawn-coloured cat at Strabane
summary: A large fawn-coloured cat was reported at Strabane, one of several big cat reports from the town since 2004.

title: Felicity the puma trapped at Cannich
summary: A farmer testing a neighbour's big cat sightings caught a female puma in a cage trap. Experts judged her a tame former pet and she lived out her life at the Highland Wildlife Park.

title: Fen Tiger seen behind Abbotsley golf club
summary: A woman walking three dogs with her partner saw a Labrador-sized brown or black cat with a feline tail, which ran off; she reported it to police. The Fen Tiger has been reported in the area for decades.

title: Fifty little figures dance and vanish into hillside, Cwmdwr
place: Cwmdwr, opposite Maestwynog farm, Llanwrda–Lampeter road, Carmarthenshire
summary: Around 2pm one day in August 1862, waggoners David Evans and Evan Lewis saw about fifty small, identically dressed figures walk up a hillside path. The figures danced in a circle, spiralled 'like a gimlet screw' and vanished into the ground, then reappeared once before vanishing again. Ceredig Davies interviewed both men.

title: Filey Brigg five saucers
summary: A local investigator reported five saucer-shaped objects in a row over the sea, then a flash and bang as an RAF aircraft passed. RAF Leeming said he had seen a heat-seeking flare.

title: Fireball in the Ogwen Valley
summary: At 5.15pm a witness saw a shooting-star-like object with a burning tail, about the size of a military jet, apparently falling towards the ground.

title: Fireman Jack of the Old Fire Station
place: Old Fire Station (Chez Jules), Northgate Street, Chester
summary: In the 1960s a bearded phantom fireman in a brass helmet was seen sitting on a ladder; the witness rang the alarm bell and quit soon after.

title: Fishermen meet tawny puma at Gimblet Rock
summary: Three men fishing saw a brown or tawny animal about the size of a golden retriever, which they thought was a puma. Another man and his son abandoned a barbecue at the same spot in May after seeing a similar cat.

title: Flat-capped worker at Cammell Laird
summary: A man in a flat cap and blue overalls is reported in the Construction Hall and an elderly woman near the kitchen. Staff have also described lights and doors operating by themselves and men in boiler suits vanishing.

title: Flat WWI sergeant on the Birkenhead train
summary: A strangely two-dimensional soldier with sergeant's stripes, a thin moustache and a swagger stick rides trains from Birkenhead Central and steps off at James Street. A lollipop man told Slemen he saw it in the 1990s with other passengers.

title: Floating sailor of the Punch Bowl, Sefton
place: Punch Bowl Inn and churchyard, Sefton
summary: A drowned sailor in blue, said to have been laid out in the inn before burial, floats about the building, sometimes just head and shoulders over a mist; he was also seen 'digging' in the churchyard.

title: Four walkers watched by cat on Moel Hiraddug
summary: Four hill walkers said a black animal, possibly a puma, stared at them for a couple of minutes before vanishing into gorse.

title: Fraserburgh trawler radar disc
summary: Four trawler crew reported a flat, shiny round object hovering about 19 miles north-east of Fraserburgh, briefly tracked on the boat's radar before it vanished. No explanation was given.

title: Fyvie fast white lights
summary: A local reporter counted 16 fast white lights crossing the sky over two nights. RAF Kinloss reported no aircraft; satellites were suggested but considered unusual in that number.

title: Gaiety Theatre seat B14
place: Gaiety Theatre, Harris Promenade, Douglas, Isle of Man
summary: An elderly woman is said to appear near seat B14 and walk through a wall.

title: Galloway Puma springs at dog walker
summary: A young woman near the golf course said a black cat bigger than an Alsatian leapt out at her and fled when her dog barked, adding to late-1990s rumours of a Galloway Puma around Kirroughtree.

title: Ghost ship at St Catherine's Island, Tenby
summary: Legend from early in Elizabeth I's reign tells of a strange ship with lights and ghostly figures in its rigging running aground by the island in a storm with no one at the helm, followed by a confessed pirate haunted by his victims leaping from the cliffs. Folklore, as retold.

title: Glamis Castle legends
summary: A chapel seat is kept empty for a White Lady thought to be Janet Douglas, and legends tell of a hidden 'monster' and of Earl Beardie gambling with the Devil.

title: Glan Conwy H-shaped light formation
summary: In summer 1983 people saw amber oval lights, then a large H-shaped formation that released smaller lights before folding in on itself and vanishing. Researchers linked it to a wave of sightings over the Clwydian Range, Prestatyn, Meliden and Dyserth in 1985-86.

title: Glaring stranger at the Slaughter House pub
summary: In 2002 the landlord watched a man walk across the closed bar, glaring at him, then vanish. Later owners report a dark shadow on the back stairs and a lift bell ringing at 2am; Most Haunted visited in 2016.

title: Glasgow West End floating figures
summary: Children playing in the street reported several figures in long white garments floating above the ground. No explanation was offered.

title: Glasgow Westbourne Gardens disc
summary: A resident reported a silver disc approaching his flat and hovering around 100 ft up, with residents of two neighbouring flats backing his account. No explanation was given.

title: Glounthaune golden light
summary: Locals saw a bright golden ball of light move very fast, change direction abruptly and disappear. No explanation was given.

title: Glowing monks and singing, Norton Priory
summary: A trespasser on the priory ruins said he heard beautiful singing and saw a pair of glowing monks.

title: Glowing triangle filmed over Buckley
summary: At about 10.30am a resident filmed a triangular object, red on top with a pulsing blue-green light underneath. Over about 20 minutes it hung still, drifted east, then turned west and climbed out of sight. He said he was not claiming it was a UFO.

title: Golden car vanishing into Queensway Tunnel wall
summary: Drivers have described a golden, futuristic-looking vehicle overtaking at huge speed and disappearing into the tunnel wall, alongside an old 1960s-style police car seen in the early hours. Slemen lists the tunnel as a timeslip spot.

title: Golden 'leopard cat' shot at, Crewood Hall Farm
summary: A farmer said he fired at a large golden cat on his land.

title: Golden Lion ploughman, Rossett
place: The Golden Lion, Chester Road, Rossett, Wrexham
summary: The pub is said to be haunted by Jeffrey, a ploughman hanged for murder and gibbeted nearby, who is blamed for moving bottles and overturning glasses and chairs, especially in bedroom two.

title: Golden spectre of Bryn yr Ellyllon, Mold
summary: Locals told of a giant figure glittering in gold seen on the burial mound for years before workmen dug up the Bronze Age Mold gold cape there in 1833. A former servant said she saw it 14 years earlier. The ghost is said not to have been seen since.

title: Grace the doll at Nantclwyd y Dre
place: Nantclwyd y Dre, Castle Street, Ruthin, Denbighshire
summary: During a 2018 ghost hunt at Ruthin's timber-framed town house, guests reported nausea, fainting and burning eyes. A doll used as a trigger object fell from its chair and moved out of a chalk circle. The doll is now kept at Tatton Old Hall.

title: Green lady seen by cadets, Sefton
place: Fields by St Helen's Church, Sefton
summary: At 2.30am one summer night at least four army cadets saw a legless green lady in an old-fashioned dress float across the fields towards the church.

title: Grey cat on A548 at Tanlan, Talacre
summary: On New Year's Eve a dark grey, Labrador-sized cat was reported beside the A548 where the national speed limit begins. An earlier report came from near Mostyn on New Year's Day 2015.

title: Greystones growing orange light
summary: A motionless orange light was reported growing to several times its size, turning red and blue, then moving west. No explanation was given.

title: Growl from the dark on Snowdon's Pyg Track
summary: A walker on the path at about 3.45am heard a loud growl from a sheltered spot and saw a brown or tawny big cat. She switched off her head torch and kept silent.

title: Gwen of the Ogofau: lost in the gold mine, seen as mist
place: Ogofau, Dolaucothi gold mines, Pumsaint, Carmarthenshire
summary: Legend says five saints sleep inside the Roman gold workings until Arthur returns. A curious woman, Gweno, who went to spy on them (or passed the limit while bathing at the well) was lost in the mine. On stormy, moonlit nights her spirit is said to hover over the crag 'Clochdy Gwenno' like a wreath of mist, and her moans are heard.

title: Gwrych Castle countess and window figure
summary: A floating woman in white, said to be the Countess of Dundonald, is reported mostly in her tower. A 2010 photo reportedly shows a pale figure at a banqueting-hall window where there was no floor to stand on. Staff describe footsteps and gate chains rattling at night.

title: Gwrych Castle White Woman
summary: A floating woman in white, linked to the Countess of Dundonald, has been reported since the 1950s, mostly around the Countess's Tower. In 2010 a prospective buyer photographed a pale figure at a banqueting hall window where the floor had rotted away.

title: Gwydir Castle ghost dog and grey lady
summary: In 1995 workmen found an old dog skeleton under the cellar floor, and a phantom dog has been reported since. A grey lady, preceded by a smell of decay, is linked to a maid said to have been walled up in the north wing.

title: Gwyllgi hound near Ruthin
summary: Writer T Gwynn Jones recorded in 1930 that his grandmother's horse shied as a huge mastiff-like dog passed on the road home from Ruthin, unseen by her husband. A former yeomanry sergeant also described a Gwyllgi trailing him over the moors from Cynwyd fair in the 1920s.

title: Hack Green Nuclear Bunker
place: Hack Green Secret Nuclear Bunker, near Nantwich, Cheshire
summary: Visitors and staff describe a young woman's apparition, an aggressive male presence and a man in period uniform.

title: Hairy giant at Castle Ring, Cannock Chase
summary: A witness described a seven-foot figure with short dark hair and glowing red eyes for about eight seconds at the hillfort. A 1995 motorist on the Cannock-Rugeley road reported a similar hairy man-like figure.

title: Hand Hotel Chirk grey lady
summary: Reported ghosts include a lady in grey called Sarah, her brother Albert, a figure by the organ, and a former employee who took his own life.

title: Harriet of Charleville Castle
summary: A girl named Harriet, said to have died falling on the stairs in 1861, is reported screaming, laughing and singing at night.

title: Haven Fort Hotel: light shuttling to Stack Rocks
place: St Brides Bay, viewed from Haven Fort Hotel, Little Haven
summary: A few nights after her landing sighting, Rose Granville reported a light moving up and down the coast and to and from Stack Rocks for 45 minutes or more.

title: Haven Fort Hotel: procession of lights over St Brides Bay
place: Haven Fort Hotel, Little Haven, Pembrokeshire
summary: Hayden Granville and hotel guests reported a procession of lights over St Brides Bay, which he likened to a train in the sky, a few nights before Rose Granville's landing report.

title: Haven Fort Hotel: Rose Granville's landed craft and two figures
place: Haven Fort Hotel, Little Haven, Pembrokeshire
summary: In the early hours Rose (Rosa) Granville, who ran the Haven Fort Hotel, heard a buzzing and saw a brightly lit oval or 'upside-down saucer' in the neighbouring field, with two tall humanoid figures in whitish or silver suits with long arms and blank faces apparently searching or measuring the ground. She reported a flattened, scorched patch nearby, close to a Royal Observer Corps bunker, and wrote to her MP Nicholas Edwards; a Squadron Leader from RAF Brawdy visited and reportedly asked the family to keep quiet. A Round Table member later claimed spacesuit pranks at the hotel and Ripperston, though Granville's daughter said a fancy-dress outing was months apart from the sighting.

title: Haverfordwest 'Harvest' abduction claim
summary: A Pembrokeshire woman, 'Susan', claimed she and others were abducted and 'harvested' by an alien intelligence in 2009, beginning in a barn; her account is told in G. L. Davies's book Harvest: The True Story of Alien Abduction. The reviewer places it in Haverfordwest; the exact site is not given.

title: Headless horse on Springwood Avenue
summary: Two teenage joggers heard hooves behind them and turned to see a headless horse's body draped in something like a tablecloth, which had gone when they looked again.

title: Headless Royalist of Tudor House
place: Tudor House, Lower Bridge Street, Chester
summary: A Royalist soldier decapitated by a cannon ball while lodging here is said to haunt the house, along with a grey lady.

title: Headless woman of Hockenhull
place: Bridle path from Hockenhull Hall, near Tarvin
summary: A servant beheaded by Cromwell's men for hiding her master's treasure walks the old path; she appeared so often that the nearby inn took the name Headless Woman.

title: Headmaster's ghost at Oldershaw, Wallasey
summary: A figure in a headmaster's gown, called Mr McGraw, was seen and heard; one cleaner persuaded the caretaker to arm himself with a pistol and search.

title: Heathrow controllers' boomerang
summary: Two air traffic controllers reported a black inverted-boomerang-shaped object seen from the control tower in the morning. No explanation is recorded in the released file.

title: Hellhound of Brereton
summary: A driver crossing the Chase reported a falling light followed by a huge black dog; a couple later described a misty figure crossing Coal Pit Lane, Brereton, in 1985.

title: Henfield police lights and beam
summary: Two Horsham police officers reported lights in the sky and a beam shining down to the ground. No explanation was given.

title: Henrietta at the Blue Bell window
place: Blue Bell Inn, Northgate Street, Chester
summary: Henrietta killed herself in the cellar after learning her Royalist lover died at Rowton Moor; her figure climbs to an upstairs window to wait for him.

title: Hessle Road silent cigar
summary: Three witnesses watched a cigar-shaped object with two red lights travel silently over the area at a slow, airship-like pace. No explanation was given.

title: Hexham wolf livestock killings
summary: A wolf blamed for livestock deaths roamed the Hexham area in the winter of 1904. It was later linked to the wolf-man figures reported in connection with the Hexham Heads in the 1970s.

title: Hindley police sighting
summary: Two police officers on duty reported a large white object in the sky. No explanation was recorded.

title: Hoghton Tower Green Lady
place: Hoghton Tower, Hoghton, near Preston, Lancashire
summary: Staff keep a file of incidents; the most frequent is a Green Lady in velvet, with a little girl, a monk and a black dog also reported.

title: Holyhead hovering white object
summary: A round, bright white object hovered and then moved slowly and quietly from south-west to north-east in the afternoon. No explanation was given.

title: Holyhead pulsating light
summary: A bright star-like light pulsing red and green hung stationary in the morning before moving away. MoD files record no explanation.

title: Hooded monks of Conwy Castle
summary: Two robed and hooded monks are said to drift along the walls, turrets and quayside and are seen as omens of disaster. Dogs reportedly refuse to pass the castle gate.

title: Houghton gravel cone and upside-down saucer
summary: Mrs Miller heard a loud whistling-sucking noise at 3:30am and next morning found road gravel heaped into a cone; she also reported a silver upside-down saucer with an orange light.

title: Howden Moor booms and triangle
summary: Two sonic booms were recorded and a large search for a crashed aircraft found nothing, with a triangular UFO reported an hour earlier. The RAF denied any supersonic flights.

title: Howden Moor phantom aircraft
place: Howden Reservoir and moors, Upper Derwent, South Yorkshire/Derbyshire
summary: On 24 March 1997 police, gamekeepers and farmers reported a low, lit aircraft and an explosion; a search across 40 square miles found no wreckage.

title: Hugh Gray's first Nessie photograph
summary: Hugh Gray's blurred image near Foyers was the first claimed photograph of the monster. Analysts have suggested it shows his Labrador swimming with a stick, or an otter.

title: Humber Bridge shape-shifting dome
place: Humber Bridge, East Riding of Yorkshire
summary: A silver dome-shaped object was seen near the bridge appearing to change from cigar to circular shape, hover, then move off. No explanation was given.

title: Humber coast silent triangle
summary: Witnesses from Cleethorpes, Grimsby, Hull and Flamborough described a slow, silent triangular or diamond-shaped object at a few hundred feet with no contrail. No explanation was found.

title: Humming triangle over Bangor
summary: Witnesses described a triangular craft up to 200 ft across, covered in lights and making a noise like a lawnmower, before it vanished.

title: Humped creature in Loch Lomond reported to police
summary: A Glasgow family saw something large with humps swimming about 200 yards off the east shore and reported it to police in Dumbarton.

title: Huskisson's limping ghost, St James's Cemetery
place: St James's Cemetery, Hope Street, Liverpool
summary: William Huskisson MP, killed by Stephenson's Rocket in 1830, is said to limp from his mausoleum in the sunken cemetery below the Anglican Cathedral. The chalybeate spring there is linked in lore to a witch called Jenna Green.

title: Ilkley Moor alien photograph
summary: A walker said he photographed a small green figure and lost time. Near the Twelve Apostles stones.

title: 'It must have been Les' at the Royal Court
place: Royal Court Theatre, Roe Street, Liverpool
summary: A caretaker named Les is said to have fallen on the icy roof and died of exposure, and staff blame him for unexplained noises and figures in photos. A red-cardiganed old lady and a Cavalier have also been reported.

title: Joggers see lit craft over Sychnant Pass
summary: Two young joggers saw a car-sized object with coloured lights around its rim and a red light underneath hovering over the pass. It sped off over the mountain within about ten seconds, and they reported it to police.

title: John Lennon at the Mendips window
summary: Beatles fans have reported a white-suited Lennon looking out of the bedroom window of his childhood home after it was restored by the National Trust. One fan claimed a night-vision camera caught a figure at the window.

title: Josephine Hewison's three-tiered craft at Lower Broadmoor Farm
place: Lower Broadmoor Farm, near Little Haven, Pembrokeshire
summary: Farmer's wife Josephine Hewison reported a three-tiered, aluminium-coloured object about 15 ft high and 35-40 ft wide standing in a field, which vanished within a minute. The family pony was later found 400 yards away. Lower Broadmoor neighbours Ripperston, where Coombs cattle were reportedly 'teleported'.

title: Keighley level crossing burns
place: Level crossing near Keighley, West Yorkshire
summary: Investigator Russ Kellett said a bright light hovered over him while he waited on his motorbike, leaving red marks on his hands, neck and face. No explanation was given.

title: Kellas cat caught on the Kellas estate
summary: A BBC Tomorrow's World team caught a live female of the large black 'Kellas cat' after a gamekeeper had snared one in 1984. Museum study showed the animals are wildcat-domestic cat hybrids.

title: Kells lights and triangle
summary: Strange lights and shapes were reported above the town for several hours, including a large triangular craft trailing multicoloured light. No explanation was given.

title: Kersey time slip
summary: Three naval cadets walked into a village that looked medieval, silent and empty, then found it normal when they returned.

title: Keyingham spearhead lights
summary: A family driving through Holderness saw three lights flying in a spearhead formation, one in front and two behind. No explanation was given.

title: Kilmainham Gaol
summary: Unseen presences are said to switch the chapel lights on and off and slam cell doors.

title: Kingstanding blue triangle residue
summary: A man reported a 200 ft blue triangle hovering over his garden at 4am before shooting away, leaving a white substance on trees that he collected. The MoD file gives no explanation.

title: Knowsley Hall banshee and phantom cars
summary: A wailing woman in white with dark eye sockets is said to roam the grounds around 4am, and two driverless vintage cars with glaring headlamps haunt the estate roads. A Welsh paranormal group photographed an 'orb' there in 2009.

title: Labrador-sized black cat crosses road, Colwyn Heights
summary: A couple driving uphill saw a big black cat about the size of a Labrador, with a long black tail, cross in front of their car. They reported it to Puma Watch North Wales.

title: Lady Blackbird of Marford
summary: Marford's cottages have cross-shaped windows said to ward off evil. The village's best-known ghost is Lady Margaret Blackbourne, said to have been murdered by her husband in 1713.

title: Lady Grey of Ruthin Castle
summary: Guests and staff report a wild-looking woman with an axe in the corridors, banqueting hall and battlements, said to be a medieval lady who killed her husband's lover. A one-gloved soldier and a giggling girl who knocks on doors are also described.

title: Lady Mary of Speke Hall
summary: Visitors to the Tudor manor report footsteps, a baby crying and a shadowy figure. The haunting is linked to a legend that a lady of the house killed her infant and then herself after her husband's gambling losses.

title: Lady of Llyn y Fan Fach and the Physicians of Myddfai
place: Llyn y Fan Fach, near Myddfai, Carmarthenshire
summary: A Myddfai farmer marries a woman who rises from Llyn y Fan Fach, on condition he never strikes her three times. When he does, she returns to the lake with all her cattle. Her sons became the Physicians of Myddfai, a real line of medieval healers.

title: Lady with candlestick on Nanteos stairs before a death
summary: An army officer staying at Nanteos said he met a woman in evening dress carrying a candlestick on the stairs. The account says Edward Powell died that night. The ghost is often linked to the 'Grey Lady' Elizabeth Owen, who died in 1757 and is said to search for hidden jewels.

title: Ladybower phantom Lancaster
summary: In October 1982 a couple in a layby saw a Lancaster-type bomber over the moonlit reservoir vanish before their eyes; another couple later reported a silent four-engined bomber by the viaduct.

title: Lakenheath–Bentwaters radar-visual case
summary: USAF and RAF radar operators tracked a number of fast-moving targets and an RAF Venom pilot sent to intercept reported a luminous object on radar and visually. It remains officially unexplained.

title: Lamb carcass stripped in barn, Ruthin
summary: A caller told North Wales Police that a dead lamb left in a barn overnight had been stripped to the bone, and linked it to a big cat. Police looked into it but the outcome was not recorded.

title: Lancaster Castle
summary: The castle, site of the 1612 witch trials and later a prison, has reports of shadowy figures, cold spots and crying.

title: Lantern Jaw and the pyramid ghost, Rodney Street
summary: Slemen counts over forty ghosts on Rodney Street, including a caped, top-hatted figure called Lantern Jaw and a shorter man linked to William Mackenzie's pyramid tomb in St Andrew's churchyard, who are seen to argue. Phantom carriages are also heard.

title: Large black cat seen leaving shed disturbance, Pontrhydfendigaid
summary: In the early 1990s a man in Pontrhydfendigaid (a friend of a BBC cameraman) said he saw a large black cat leaving the scene after a disturbance near his shed. This is a separate report from the 1981 Bont sheep killings.

title: Large cat crossing A5 near Chirk
summary: Rural police received a report of a larger-than-usual cat crossing the A5 between Chirk and Llangollen in the early hours, and asked the public not to approach any such animal.

title: Large object followed by helicopter, Old Colwyn
summary: At about 2.30am a silent object bigger than a helicopter, with a bar-like part, was seen roughly 250 m up. After about half a minute it headed out over the sea with a helicopter close behind.

title: Leap Castle Red Lady
place: Leap Castle, near Roscrea, Co Offaly
summary: Known for its Bloody Chapel and an 'elemental' publicised by Mildred Darby, the castle also reports a dagger-carrying Red Lady and two girls.

title: Lennoxtown coloured beam
place: Glen Road, near Lennoxtown, East Dunbartonshire
summary: Three people in a car reported being lit by a coloured beam for more than two minutes. No explanation was given.

title: Leopard-marked cat at the Cow and Calf
place: Cow and Calf rocks, Ilkley Moor, West Yorkshire
summary: A Leeds University student and friends saw a very muscular cat with leopard-like markings on a rock about 20 metres away; another group of men also saw it. He photographed the animal.

title: Letham phantom battle
place: near Letham, below Dunnichen Hill, Angus
summary: Walking home at about 2am on 2 January 1950, Miss E.F. Smith reported torch-bearing figures searching for bodies in fields, later linked to the 685 battle of Nechtanesmere.

title: Lioness reported at Upton
summary: A lioness was reported roaming the Upton area of Chester; police searched but found nothing.

title: Little girl on the Queen Hotel's second floor
place: The Queen Hotel, City Road, Chester, Cheshire
summary: A girl is said to appear on the second floor, where a nursery once was. Guests report hearing her tricycle at night and having their hair tugged while running baths.

title: Little Orme purple triangle and missing time
summary: A family driving at night said a purple triangular craft engulfed their car and they lost several hours. The driver later said a small black object fell from his mouth, and that air force personnel told the family to keep quiet.

title: Liverpool Empire Theatre girl
place: Liverpool Empire Theatre, Lime Street, Liverpool
summary: A tearful Victorian girl has been seen in the bars, and a dark apparition in a dressing room reportedly stopped once the room became a store.

title: Llancaiach Fawr Manor
summary: The Tudor manor was listed among the UK's top haunted places in 2007; a Wales Online journalist spent a night there in 2018 and described four spirits it is said to host.

title: Llanddewi Brefi: rising hill, bellowing ox and church-moving spirit
summary: Tradition says the ground rose under St David as he preached at the Synod of Brefi in 519. A Bannog ox bellowed nine times and split Foelallt rock, and a spirit pulled down by night the church begun at Godregarth farm. A horn core said to be the ox's, identified as aurochs, was long kept at the church.

title: Llandudno Easter-egg object
summary: A couple described an egg-shaped object gliding and jumping above their home before turning spherical and speeding into cloud; weeks later they reported a ball of light over the Orme cliffs. No explanation was given.

title: Llanerchymedd silver figures in a field
summary: A farmer out shooting saw a bright white light come down slowly. Soon afterwards a mother at her window saw three tall figures in silver-grey suits walking across a field as cows stampeded. A catalogue review rates the case weak and suggests firefighters in protective suits.

title: Llanfyllin four-colour disc
summary: Concert-goers reported a disc-shaped object in blue, green, white and orange moving slowly up and down. MoD files record no explanation.

title: Llangefni bedroom ball of light
summary: The wife of a retired Royal Marine said a light came into her bedroom, its surface pulsing as if with energy, and later left through the window.

title: Llannefydd colour-changing spheres
summary: A local shop manager filmed pulsing, colour-changing spheres over his property over several weeks, once counting 13 in a night. Police passed it to the MoD, which gave no explanation.

title: Llyn Cefni fireball
summary: A fireball or meteorite was reported plunging into the reservoir, according to MoD files. No confirmed explanation was recorded.

title: Loftus Hall card game
place: Loftus Hall, Hook Peninsula, Co Wexford
summary: Legend says Anne Tottenham saw a cloven foot on a card-playing stranger who vanished through the roof; she declined and died in 1775 and is said to haunt the house.

title: Long-tailed black cat at Treuddyn
summary: At 2.35am a resident watched a large black cat with a tail several feet long cross a paddock about 100 yards away for a couple of minutes. Horses in the paddock seemed undisturbed.

title: Long-tailed cat and paw print, Ince Marshes
summary: A worker arriving at dawn saw a large, slender cat-like animal with a very long tail. Later that morning he photographed a possible paw print in mud about 300 metres away.

title: Longdendale lights
summary: Long tradition of lights on Bleaklow and the Devil's Elbow, alongside ghostly aircraft stories from the many crash sites.

title: Longhill Park egg-shaped landing
summary: Children reported a silver egg-shaped object landing in the park and lifting off silently as they ran towards it. A small helicopter was suggested but never confirmed.

title: Lorry driver sees big cat at Llangadog creamery
summary: Shortly after the Llangadog dog killing, a lorry driver saw a big cat in his headlights at the creamery in the early hours of a Wednesday.

title: Lough Foyle 'monster' video
summary: College students filming a class project posted a clip of a dark object moving on the surface and diving. Critics suggested a marine animal and questioned whether the footage was staged.

title: Lough Ree monster seen by three priests
summary: Three priests fishing on the lough watched an animal roughly six feet long with a head about 18 inches across from about 100 yards away. The story was carried locally and later by the BBC.

title: Louth triangle seen by many
summary: Numerous witnesses reported a large triangular craft with three lights that hovered, rotated and shot upwards at speed. The MoD file gives no explanation.

title: Lynx captured at Drumguish
summary: Two lynx believed to have been illegally released were caught in bait traps and taken to the Highland Wildlife Park; two more were seen in the area the next day.

title: Lynx-like animal on Mold Road, Gwersyllt
summary: A witness reported an animal resembling a lynx at the roadside on Mold Road near Wrexham. Police investigated without finding it.

title: Lynx of the links, Eyemouth
summary: A dog walker thought he saw a lynx on the golf course, and three more people later came forward with similar accounts.

title: Mablethorpe hovering oblong
summary: A bright oblong object with a rounded end was reported hovering silently over the coast. No explanation was given.

title: Mackays see whale-like creature, Loch Ness
summary: A couple driving the new A82 saw a whale-bodied animal rolling in the loch. Its report in the Inverness Courier popularised the word 'monster' and began the modern Nessie story.

title: Mackenzie Poltergeist, Greyfriars
summary: Visitors near Sir George Mackenzie's Black Mausoleum report scratches, burns and fainting, and the area is generally locked except for tours.

title: Man in black in room 6, Ye Olde King's Head
place: Ye Olde King's Head, Lower Bridge Street, Chester, Cheshire
summary: In 1982 a guest in room 6 watched a silent man in black for about 15 minutes. Other reports include a child spirit, writing appearing on the room 4 mirror, and items vanishing. A sword found under a room 4 floorboard hangs on the wall.

title: Marching legion under the George and Dragon
place: George and Dragon, Liverpool Road, Chester
summary: The pub stands on the line of the Roman road out of the fortress, and landlords and drinkers have reported marching feet in the cellars following the old route. The pub closed in 2023.

title: Mark Marston chased by a silver-suited giant, Herbrandston
summary: Schoolboy Mark Marston (spelled Marsden in some accounts), aged 11-12, said a red glow appeared and a figure in a silver diver-like suit with a square featureless helmet drifted through a gate and came rapidly towards him, so he ran home screaming. Some accounts add that he and his father found a large treadless bootprint the next day. Dated Easter Monday 11 April 1977 by Cambria Stories; HUMCAT files it under 20 April; investigated by Randall Jones Pugh for BUFORA.

title: Marston Moor Cavaliers
place: Marston Moor, Long Marston, North Yorkshire
summary: In November 1932 two friends driving across the battlefield saw three men in Cavalier-style cloaks and hats who vanished as the car slowed; a group of tourists reported similar 17th-century figures in 1968.

title: Mary King's Close
place: Mary King's Close, Royal Mile, Edinburgh
summary: The buried 17th-century close has a long haunting reputation and has been investigated repeatedly; one suggestion is that marsh gas from the Nor Loch caused eerie lights.

title: Melanistic leopard seen by runner, Llysfaen
summary: A man out running saw a huge black animal he took to be a melanistic leopard; the same day a dog walker at nearby Bryn Cadno reported a fast-moving puma.

title: Melinda Messenger's golden orbs over the sea
summary: TV presenter Melinda Messenger posted video of 'golden sun sized orbs' over the sea horizon that appeared repeatedly, forming lines and triangles. Metabunk analysts matched them to illumination flares from the Castlemartin range, noting the conflict with her stated north-Pembrokeshire location; coordinates approximate (Castlemartin coast).

title: Menock Road floating carriage
summary: A man at a bus stop reported a railway-carriage-shaped object with three windows and swirling yellow smoke passing about 20 ft overhead, and a sense that time had stood still. No explanation was given.

title: Mermaid of Cemaes Head
place: Cemaes Head, near St Dogmaels, Pembrokeshire
summary: Eighteenth-century tale of fisherman Peregrine, who caught and released a mermaid on a cliff crag in exchange for warnings; she later urged him ashore before a storm that drowned other fishermen. Folklore, as retold.

title: Middlesbrough silent triangle
summary: An eastbound triangular object was reported sweeping silently overhead in the evening. No explanation was given.

title: Midnight phantom funeral, Knotty Ash
summary: A witness watched a silent midnight funeral pass, complete with coffin and deathly pale mourners, and later learned a secret funeral had once set out from a nearby hall.

title: Mile-long saucer over Anfield
summary: Lee Jones, his wife and her mother watched a vast saucer hover, partly hidden by cloud; a passing airliner let him estimate it at a mile across. Others reported it earlier that year.

title: Milntown, Ramsey
place: Milntown, near Ramsey, Isle of Man
summary: Called the island's most haunted house, it is said to host a former lady of the house and a hostile spirit.

title: Moddey Dhoo of Peel Castle
place: Peel Castle, St Patrick's Isle, Peel, Isle of Man
summary: A phantom black dog is said to haunt the castle; in Waldron's 1731 account a drunken guard who went alone through its passage returned speechless and died days later.

title: Moelfre lantern-like UFO
summary: National Archives papers record a UFO over Moelfre described as looking like a Chinese lantern, which is the likely explanation.

title: Moigns Down 'girder' craft
summary: Angus Brooks reported watching a translucent craft with movable girder-like arms hover for about 22 minutes on the downs. No explanation was given.

title: Monk and lunging figure at the Liverpool Arms
place: Liverpool Arms, Lower Gate Street, Conwy
summary: A landlady saw a monk kneeling in prayer in the tower room in 1980, just after a family accident. In 1991 a barman said a very tall figure with a small boy lunged at him. The monk is said to warn of bad news.

title: Morag of Loch Morar
summary: Reports of a serpent-like animal date from 1887, with 34 incidents counted by 1981. In the best-known case two local men said their boat struck a 25-30 ft humped creature, which they fended off with an oar and a rifle shot.

title: Muckie sonar contact, Lakes of Killarney
summary: Scientists surveying fish with sonar recorded a large solid object, prompting talk of a lake monster nicknamed Muckie. Seals surfacing in pairs have been suggested as an explanation for sightings.

title: Murdered miller at Bidston Windmill
summary: A misty outline of a man, said to be a miller murdered in the early 1800s, has been reported many times around the windmill on Bidston Hill. Local lore also ties the hill to covens and a buried occultist named Richard Tilly.

title: Mystery light on Cadair Idris ridge
summary: A resident reported a bright, stationary light high on the ridge above the Tal-y-llyn pass, and 16 rescue volunteers went out. Through binoculars they found that trees on the ridge had been hung with solar fairy lights.

title: Nantclwyd y Dre White Lady
place: Nantclwyd y Dre, Castle Street, Ruthin, Denbighshire
summary: Since the 15th-century timbered town house opened as a museum in 2007, staff and visitors have reported a lady in white and poltergeist activity. Investigators also linked a spirit to a doll known as Grace.

title: Nanteos Cup: Strata Florida 'Holy Grail' healing cup
place: Strata Florida Abbey and Nanteos Mansion, Ceredigion
summary: Tradition says monks brought a wooden cup (claimed as the Holy Grail or made from the True Cross) to Strata Florida, and that after the Dissolution it passed via the Stedmans to the Powells of Nanteos. People borrowed it as a healing cup, and Ceredig Davies says some patients bit pieces off it. It is now in the National Library of Wales.

title: Ness mid-air explosion
summary: Residents reported a mid-air explosion, prompting a search by an RAF Nimrod and helicopters. Nothing was found and no explanation was given.

title: Newbiggin radar guard beam claim
summary: A wartime radar guard, Albert Lancaster, later claimed he had been caught in a beam and felt himself floating while on duty near the coast. No explanation is recorded.

title: Newsham Park Hospital
place: Newsham Park Hospital, Newsham Park, Liverpool
summary: The former orphanage and hospital has reports of a nurse's apparition, child ghosts and banging from old punishment cupboards.

title: Northallerton black triangle
summary: A black triangular object with green lights was reported over the town. No explanation was given.

title: Old woman drawn by Reginald Easton, Thurstaston
summary: Artist Reginald Easton woke to an old woman by his bed and stayed a week to sketch her; she is said to have murdered a child at the hall.

title: Orange ball emerges from Stack Rock
place: Stack Rocks, St Brides Bay, Pembrokeshire
summary: Unnamed locals reported an orange ball with two dark lines emerging from Stack Rock between 1:30 and 2am, oscillating, shrinking and vanishing.

title: Orange ball over Mersey and Dee from Wallasey Docks
