summary: A night-shift crew at a dockside mill watched a fuzzy orange ball hang over Liverpool Bay, dart across to hover over the Dee, then shoot upwards and vanish. The witness recalls the Liverpool Echo reporting many calls from along the coast.

title: Orange light over Denbigh Hospital
summary: In summer 1974 two women leaving the old psychiatric hospital saw a round, bright orange light that shot away at great speed. Similar lights were reported over the Denbigh Moors in 1984 and 1994.

title: Orange light seen from Mynydd Mechell
summary: On New Year's Eve a father and son watched a bright orange light, which they judged much brighter than the ISS, vanish and reappear on a steady track for two to three minutes. The RAF referred them to a UFO hotline the MoD had just closed.

title: Orange lights from Puffin Island direction
summary: Over several weeks a Benllech resident saw fuzzy, non-pulsing orange lights rise over the sea from the direction of Beaumaris and Puffin Island. On 8 August three moved together, and a fourth crossed her view, shrank and vanished.

title: Orange lights over Caerwys pubs
summary: Drinkers at the Piccadilly Inn and the Royal Oak went outside to watch bright orange circular lights crossing the sky one Wednesday evening. One self-described sceptic said he could not explain what he saw.

title: Orange sphere over Cardigan
summary: At about 7:30pm Mrs G. James of Finch Square and Miss M. Mathews reported a perfect round orange sphere with no tail and no noise over Cardigan.

title: Oval object on Conwy Mountain
summary: A retired post office engineer from Llandudno was walking in a gale when he saw an oval object, white on top and dark underneath. It stopped, moved on, and disappeared into a glow.

title: Owlman of Mawnan
summary: Children reported a large owl-like man-creature above the church tower.

title: Panther hunting on Ffrith Beach
summary: Around 6am a dog walker saw a black panther-like cat chasing rabbits and birds before it ran fast across the beach.

title: Pauline Coombs chased by a glowing 'flying football'
place: Lane to Ripperston Farm (Dale road near St Ishmaels), Pembrokeshire
summary: Driving home at night with three of her children, Pauline Coombs reported a yellowish, rugby-ball-sized object with a torch-like beam that followed and hovered over the car; the headlamps failed and the engine died near the farm, and the family ran into the house. Her husband Billy and son Clinton said they saw it head out to sea. The Western Telegraph headlined it 'Chased by a Flying Football'; dates given range from spring to May-June 1977, and coordinates are approximate (farm lane).

title: Pauline Coombs' reported abduction
summary: Pauline Coombs came to believe she had been taken aboard a craft during the months of activity at Ripperston, as recounted in Clive Harold's book The Uninvited (1979) and later retellings. The claim is as reported; no independent corroboration is given.

title: Paw prints in snow on Pen-y-ghent
summary: Walkers descending Pen-y-ghent photographed a trail of large, fresh prints in snow. A British Big Cats Society researcher judged from the photos that they could be from a puma or lynx.

title: Pendle Hill witches
summary: Ghosts of the 1612 Pendle witches are said to roam the hill, and during a live Most Haunted broadcast on Halloween 2004 team members at a nearby farmhouse reported choking sensations.

title: Pentyrch pyramid of light
summary: Witnesses described a pyramid of light descending and releasing objects, followed by military aircraft and explosions. The MoD said it was a routine exercise but withheld some details.

title: Penuwch ewe eviscerated, heart removed
summary: In 2015 a Penuwch farmer found a ewe eviscerated and dragged about 20 feet, with its heart removed. The case is cited as part of the long-running 'Beast of Bont' big-cat claims in the area.

title: Pete the Cardiff Poltergeist
place: Mower Services, Crwys Road, Cathays, Cardiff
summary: From 1979 staff at a mower shop reported thrown stones, moving tools and appearing coins; SPR investigator David Fontana studied it from 1989 to 1992.

title: Peter MacNab's humps photo, Urquhart Castle
summary: A photograph of two humps near Urquhart Castle was later attributed to wakes from trawlers, and differences between negative and print raised suspicion of doctoring.

title: Phantom battle of Edgehill
summary: Shepherds and villagers reported spectral armies re-fighting the battle around Christmas 1642, described in a January 1643 pamphlet; a royal commission was said to have witnessed it.

title: Phantom bear of the Martin Tower
place: Martin Tower, Tower of London, London
summary: In January 1816 the Keeper of the Crown Jewels described a floating apparition, and a sentry who met a bear-like shape reportedly died two days later.

title: Phantom burial service heard at Llanafan churchyard
summary: An old woman living beside Llanafan churchyard said she heard the vicar, Rev. W. J. Williams, reading the burial service distinctly from her bed one night. A funeral took place soon after, and she told the vicar herself.

title: Phantom city in the sky over Liverpool
summary: A white city briefly appeared above Liverpool; it was put down to a mirage of Edinburgh, although nobody could pick out any of its buildings.

title: Phantom harp music in Nanteos woods
summary: Harp music heard in the Nanteos woods on still nights is attributed to the Powell family harpist, said to have played there at Christmas for 69 years. A drowned man (possibly David Rowlands, d. 1899) is also said to be seen near the lake.

title: Phantom monk and candles at Strata Florida Abbey
summary: A monk's ghost is said to appear on Christmas Eve where the abbey altar stood, and candles have reportedly been seen burning inside the ruins. The churchyard yew is said to mark the grave of the poet Dafydd ap Gwilym.

title: Phantom monk outside Holywell
summary: A married couple told the Daily Post they believe they saw a monk-like ghost on the outskirts of Holywell.

title: Phantom rider in the Queensway Tunnel
summary: A pillion passenger killed in a 1960s motorbike crash is said to appear in the tunnel and make drivers swerve. A vintage police car has also reportedly been seen.

title: Phantom ship off Abergele
summary: Witnesses on the Abergele coast have described a large ship crewed by Viking-like men that vanished moments after it was seen. It is linked to the legend of Prince Madoc's lost voyage.

title: Pied Bull cellar and chambermaids
place: The Pied Bull, 57 Northgate Street, Chester, Cheshire
summary: The cellar of this old coaching inn is said to be haunted by a man who died after falling down its stairs in 1609. Two bedrooms are linked to ghostly chambermaids.

title: Piers Gaveston, Scarborough Castle
summary: The headless ghost of Piers Gaveston, beheaded in 1312, is said to appear by the barbican and on the battlements and to lure people towards the cliff edge.

title: Plas Mawr black dog and pipe smoke
summary: A volunteer saw a black dog on a landing, a small child said an angry man was in a servants' bed, and a custodian keeps smelling pipe tobacco in the gatehouse shop. A local writer reported a girl in blue and a Civil War figure in the courtyard.

title: Plas Teg haunting
summary: Jacobean house near Mold often called the most haunted house in Wales. Reports of a woman in the grounds and apparitions inside.

title: Plas yn Rhiw Victorian girl
place: Plas yn Rhiw, Rhiw, Llŷn, Gwynedd
summary: The house is reputedly haunted by a Victorian daughter of the owners who left to marry a tinker and was later abandoned.

title: Pluckley
summary: Village claimed to have a dozen or more resident ghosts, including a highwayman and a screaming man.

title: Pointy-eared cat runs past car, Hafan y Mor
place: Hafan y Mor holiday park, Pwllheli, Gwynedd
summary: A mother and her teenage daughter driving through the holiday park at about 2am saw a large pointy-eared animal, too big for a fox, run in front of the car into hedges.

title: Police officers see light over Penmaenmawr
summary: An officer was sent after a member of the public reported a strange light at 9.10pm. A police inspector confirmed that officers also saw a light that grew and shrank before fading away.

title: Pont Einion: harpist returns after years among the fairies
place: Pont Einion / Ystrad Caron, Tregaron, Ceredigion
summary: Local tradition told to Ceredig Davies says Einion of Ystrad Caron, who built a bridge over the Teifi, vanished for many years among the fairies. He came back on the day his 'widow' was due to remarry and proved who he was by playing his harp. The same bridge was 'once noted for its witches': a farmer said a witch jumped onto his horse there until he drew her blood.

title: Pont Llanafan ghost: stones down chimney and treasure
place: Pont Llanafan (Llanafan bridge), Ystwyth valley, Ceredigion
summary: A farmer named Edwards near Llanafan bridge was reportedly troubled day and night by a spirit. It dropped stones down the chimney, threw ashes in his milk, threshed in the barn and pulled down his fence, until he asked it in God's name what it wanted. It was said to have shown him treasure hidden in a wall. The bridge was also said to be haunted, with a recent sighting at the time of writing (c.1911).

title: Ponterwyd: 20 sheep butchered
summary: Cambrian News lists the killing of 20 sheep near Ponterwyd in 2012 among incidents blamed by farmers on a big cat in the Cambrian Mountains.

title: Ponterwyd farmer loses skinned yearling ewes
summary: Farmer Johnathan Davies lost yearling ewes, some of them skinned, in February 2023 on a farm near Ponterwyd. He said police told him a big cat could be responsible.

title: Pool Parc stone-throwing spirit
summary: Visitors to the former manor describe an aggressive presence. Reports include stones being thrown, bruising to the face, unexplained noises and shadowy figures.

title: Pool Park former hospital
place: Pool Park, Efenechtyd, near Ruthin, Denbighshire
summary: Investigators describe an aggressive presence at the former hospital, which closed in 1989, with reports of thrown stones, unexplained bruising, noises and shadowy figures.

title: Powys Puma escapes police marksmen, Llangurig
summary: After four sheep were killed, police marksmen and RSPCA officials cornered a cat in a barn, but it escaped through a rear exit.

title: Prescot green saucer
summary: Two friends heard a loud aircraft-like noise and saw a green saucer-shaped object for a few seconds before it rose into cloud, and took photos. No explanation was given.

title: Prestwick radar target
summary: An air traffic controller tracked a fast-moving unidentified target on radar. An RAF investigation found nothing to corroborate it.

title: Puma in an Abersoch back garden
summary: A resident who had seen pumas in the Pyrenees said one stood by his shed facing him for about five seconds before running off. He called police within ten minutes.

title: Puma in the Meadows, Overton-on-Dee
summary: A local man walking his dog watched a very large cat in long grass below St Mary's House for several minutes and later identified it as a puma from pictures.

title: Puma-like cat on A96, Huntly
summary: A motorist nearly hit a jet-black, Labrador-high cat with a thick curled tail on the A96 by Huntly Industrial Estate.

title: Puma of Pontybodkin
summary: A villager saw a dog-sized black cat-shaped animal sprint across a field, and a walker filmed a large black cat crossing a lane nearby. Repeated reports led a Senedd member to call for a government investigation.

title: Puma raiding litter bin, Fochabers
summary: A driver stopping in a lay-by watched a puma-sized cat standing on its hind legs clawing at a litter bin before it slipped into undergrowth. He and his wife had seen a similar cat on the same road that July.

title: Puma reported at Limavady
summary: A puma was reported at Limavady in December 2004, following reports of large black cats there that June.

title: Python-like creature at Loch Morlich
summary: Four pupils and their teacher on a school trip saw a long snake-like shape drop into the loch; the teacher compared it to a big python.

title: RAF Boulmer radar-tracked objects
summary: An RAF flight lieutenant and two colleagues watched two luminous objects over the sea about three miles offshore for well over an hour, while base radar held them in the same position. The MoD report was released years later without an explanation.

title: RAF Valley control tower 'buzzing'
summary: An unidentified object was reported buzzing the control tower. The MoD found no record in air traffic logs and suggested a routine low-flying training sortie.

title: Rainhill landing chased by police
summary: Robert Bennett told the St Helens Star he chased a strange craft across the sky with police and radio hams; three officers watched it lift off after landing in a field.

title: Randall Jones Pugh's own sighting
summary: BUFORA investigator and vet Randall Jones Pugh, co-author with F. W. Holiday of The Dyfed Enigma (Faber 1979, Coronet 1981), described drawing back his bedroom curtains to see a crescent-shaped object with a dome and a tube in a field, which took off vertically. His home location is not given; coordinates are a generic Broad Haven-area point.

title: Red lights over Gwersyllt were helicopters
summary: Several residents saw and filmed two linked red lights moving slowly and silently over Wrexham, and similar lights were reported near Sandycroft. A reader later identified them as two Royal Navy Lynx helicopters on night-flying training.

title: Rendlesham Forest incident
summary: USAF personnel from RAF Woodbridge reported lights and a craft in the forest over several nights. Deputy base commander Charles Halt recorded a memo and audio tape.

title: Rhosmeherin moor ghost: cat and horseman
place: Rhos Meherin, near Ystrad Meurig / Pontrhydfendigaid, Ceredigion
summary: Late travellers crossing Rhosmeherin were reportedly terrified by a ghost that appeared sometimes as a cat and sometimes as a man on horseback. The haunting was blamed on the murder of an old woman there. Discover Ceredigion describes spirits on horseback galloping across the moor.

title: Rhosybol netball team sighting
summary: Nine schoolgirl netball players reported a strange object over the village and later drew what they saw, days after the Broad Haven school case. No explanation was given.

title: Rhyl large black object
summary: A large black object was reported over the town. No explanation was given.

title: Rines 'flipper' photograph, Urquhart Bay
summary: Robert Rines's expedition recorded sonar targets and an underwater 'rhomboid flipper' image. Rines later accepted the image may have been retouched.

title: Ripley Castle mourning mother
summary: A figure in 19th-century dress, said to be Lady Alicia Ingilby, walks towards the children's rooms through a locked door; Civil War soldiers shot after Marston Moor are also reported.

title: Ripperston Farm: faceless silver giant at the window
summary: While watching a late film, Billy and Pauline Coombs reported a figure over 7 ft tall in a one-piece silver suit with a blank black visor and a pipe over its shoulder at the sitting-room window, which rattled the glass; the television failed and a rose bush outside was said to be singed. Police and neighbour Mr Hewison found nothing; the attending officer later said it was the most frightened family he had seen in 26 years of service. Dated 23 April by David Clarke and 24 April by Cambria Stories.

title: Ripperston Farm: sixteen heifers vanish from a bolted yard
summary: Billy Coombs and his son Clinton reported that sixteen in-calf heifers vanished from a bolted stockyard within about four minutes, with bolts and twine intact. The Coombs said cattle were 'teleported' at least six times, typically turning up at Lower Broadmoor Farm about half a mile away; in one version Billy locked 158 cattle in the milking shed and was phoned by an angry neighbour about cows eating his crops a mile away.

title: Ripperston: tripod craft and burnt circle
summary: From her kitchen window Pauline Coombs reported a silver craft about 14-20 ft across with an antenna, resting on a tripod-like support 400-500 yards away; after it left the family found a burnt circular mark in the grass. She also described an object with a reddish-orange tail dropping into the Mount Vanor clifftop fields.

title: Rivington Pike counter-rotating rings
summary: A driver crossing Belmont reported two rotating circles of light, one inside the other, turning in opposite directions above Rivington. A similar sight had been reported over Winter Hill weeks earlier.

title: Roman sentry on Chester's walls
place: City Walls near Newgate, Chester, Cheshire
summary: A Roman soldier is said to patrol the walls between Newgate and the amphitheatre. Legend says he was murdered after leaving his post to visit a local girl.

title: Roman soldiers, Treasurer's House
summary: In 1953 apprentice plumber Harry Martindale, working in the cellar, saw a column of Roman soldiers and a horse emerge from the wall, visible only from the knees up. He repeated the account unchanged for decades.

title: Rottweiler-sized black cat, Rockcliffe
summary: A bus driver saw a shiny black cat about the height of a Rottweiler with a curled tail rise from a field, stare at the bus and run off.

title: Rowton Moor battle ghost and phantom music
summary: The 1645 Civil War battlefield is said to be visited by a fallen Royalist commander around the 24 September anniversary. Music by Charles I's court composer William Lawes, who died there, is reportedly heard across the moor.

title: Royal Goat Hotel landlord, Beddgelert
summary: The hotel's former landlord David Pritchard is said to walk its corridors.

title: Royal Oak Hotel, Betws-y-Coed
place: Royal Oak Hotel, Holyhead Road, Betws-y-Coed, Conwy
summary: Reported presences include a cloaked lady, a nun and a shadow in the bar, with staff describing TVs switching themselves on and whispered questions in corridors.

title: Rutherglen Poltergeist
summary: In August 2016 a family reported clothes thrown, lights switching and lampshades inverted, with police witnessing events.

title: Ruthin Gaol hanged prisoner
place: Ruthin Gaol, Clwyd Street, Ruthin, Denbighshire
summary: The former prison is said to be haunted by William Hughes, the only man hanged there, in 1903, for murdering his wife. Visitors report voices, slamming cell doors and being touched, and a vanished guard is also said to linger.

title: Ruthin Gaol slamming doors
place: Ruthin Gaol, Clwyd Street, Ruthin, Denbighshire
summary: Visitors report voices, being touched or pushed, and heavy cell doors slamming by themselves. The spirits are linked to William Hughes, the only man hanged there in 1903, a former guard and a young girl.

title: Rydal School fuzzy light
summary: A 17-year-old pupil heard a noise and saw a bright, fuzzy white object with flashing lights move then speed away. A local astronomer suggested a satellite, Venus or a meteor.

title: S4C film crew disturbances at Nanteos
summary: Citing a Western Mail report, the Nanteos history site says an S4C crew in the early 1980s experienced doors opening and closing, a musical box playing and a bed moving, and refused to work after dark. The same site says trained police dogs refused to enter the cellar during training in the early 1990s.

title: Salt Tower presences
place: Salt Tower, Tower of London, London
summary: Two guardsmen saw a white form on the roof in 1957, and in 1973 a Yeoman Warder reported a glow and a touch on his neck; dogs are said to avoid the tower.

title: Samlesbury Hall White Lady
place: Samlesbury Hall, Preston New Road, Samlesbury, Lancashire
summary: Dorothy Southworth, said to have died of a broken heart, is the hall's White Lady, and motorists on the nearby road have reported seeing her.

title: Sarah the poltergeist of Eastgate Street
summary: A spirit known as Sarah, said to be a jilted bride who hanged herself, is blamed for moving objects and pushing people on the stairs of this old shop. In 1991 heart-shaped chocolate boxes were reportedly found scattered across the floor.

title: Sauchie Poltergeist
summary: From 22 November 1960, knocks and moving objects centred on 11-year-old Virginia Campbell were witnessed by doctors, a minister and her teacher, at home and in class.

title: Scholes shape-changing light
summary: A woman on a flat balcony watched a floating light change shape, brighten, hover and drift out of sight. She rejected a Chinese lantern because of the shape change.

title: Screeching Ginny at Garston Dock station
summary: Children playing on the disused tracks were chased by a pale, witch-like figure that glided without moving its legs; one said her mouth opened impossibly wide. Lore names her as a jilted witch killed by a train.

title: Scunthorpe arrow of lights
summary: Between 10 and 16 very bright lights were reported travelling north at speed in an arrow formation. No explanation was given.

title: Sea vibrations and crystals in St Brides Bay
summary: Pauline Coombs reported the sea shaking with vibrations radiating from a point in the bay, and her last sighting of the 'Silver Giant', now without a visor, in her garden in February 1978. The same month reddish-brown quartz-like crystals were reported falling on St Brides Bay. Coordinates are a general point in the bay.

title: Seven-foot black shadow in Flint
summary: Around 1990-91 two friends walking home late saw a man-shaped black shadow seven or eight feet tall. Both felt a menacing presence and ran.

title: Shannon pilots' high-speed lights
summary: A British Airways pilot told Shannon air traffic control an object had passed her aircraft at very high speed off the west coast, and other pilots reported similar lights. The Irish Aviation Authority investigated and a meteor or re-entering debris was suggested.

title: Shape-shifting figure from the canal, Chester
place: Canal towpath by Griffiths' Steam Mill, Chester
summary: A walker watched a pale grey form rise from the canal, change shape and wrap him in a clammy mist before he broke free and ran.

title: Sheep stripped to skeleton, Ravensworth
summary: A sheep was found with its flesh stripped away and North Yorkshire Police's rural crime officer said the evidence fitted a possible big cat attack. Another carcass had been found days earlier at nearby Whashton.

title: Shimmering object dips into the water off Milford Haven
summary: A 93-year-old woman walking on Robert Street around 11am reported a very large, round, shimmering object over the water that dipped in and out of it, emitted cloud-like smoke from its sides, then shot off into the sky. She took no photograph.

title: Shotts panther flap
summary: A cluster of black 'panther' sightings around Shotts in early 2011 drew attention before quickly dying away.

title: Shug Monkey of Slough Hill Lane
place: Slough Hill Lane, West Wratting, Cambridgeshire
summary: A shaggy black creature with a dog's body and a monkey's face was said to haunt the lane between West Wratting and Balsham; the stories were published in 1954 and no sightings are known after the Second World War.

title: Silent phantom bomber over the A44 at Pumlumon
place: A44 near Eisteddfa Gurig, Pumlumon, Ceredigion
summary: Drivers on the A44 between Aberystwyth and Llangurig say they have seen a low-flying WW2 bomber that makes no sound. Witness Paul Jay said it appeared so suddenly he expected a crash in his mirror, but it had gone. USAAF F-5E 44-24229 crashed on Pumlumon Fawr on 11 September 1945.

title: Silpho Moor saucer with copper scrolls
summary: A small metal saucer about 18 inches across was reportedly found on moorland between Silpho and Hackness, containing thin copper sheets engraved with symbols. Its origin was never established and it is widely regarded as a hoax.

title: Silver giants on the A48 at Nantycaws Hill
summary: Lorry driver Francis Lloyd and his 16-year-old passenger John Dwyer reported two 7-ft reddish-orange figures with elongated heads and aerials beside the road; Lloyd felt a cold tingling. Some investigators later linked the spot to a fatal tanker crash there on 23 November 1977, a connection the source calls unproven. Inland Carmarthenshire, about 40 miles east of Broad Haven.

title: Silver-suited figure seen leaving a pub, Broad Haven area
summary: An unnamed neighbour reported a huge silver-suited, helmetless figure with protruding eyes after leaving a pub, around the time of the spring 1977 sightings.

title: 'Skin crawler' photographed in Coed y Cwm woods
place: Coed y Cwm, south of Clarach, near Aberystwyth, Ceredigion
summary: A reader sent Cambrian News a flash photo, saying a hairless, human-like creature moving on all fours followed them for about 45 minutes while they walked their dog. Dyfed-Powys Police found no matching report. The image's file name contained 'hoax email' and the report is unverified.

title: Small humanoid at a Milford Haven bedroom window
summary: An anonymous 17-year-old reported a 3-ft humanoid on her windowsill at 3am beside a craft emitting a green beam, and days later at 5am a smaller craft beside her father's car with an oval-faced figure.

title: Snaefell mast mystery crash
summary: Riders reported something like a microlight striking the summit mast and spiralling down in smoke, triggering a large search with an RAF helicopter. Nothing was found and no aircraft was missing.

title: Solway Firth 'spaceman' photo
summary: A fireman's photograph of his daughter on the marshes showed a white-suited figure behind her that he believed was a spaceman. Later analysis concluded it was most likely his wife seen from behind.

title: South Stack Lighthouse footsteps
place: South Stack Lighthouse, near Holyhead, Anglesey
summary: Footsteps have been reported on the stairs to the footbridge, along with cries and screams.

title: South Stack Lighthouse poltergeist
place: South Stack Lighthouse, Holy Island, Anglesey
summary: A poltergeist is said to be active at the cliff-top lighthouse, which was investigated in the ninth series of Most Haunted.

title: South Wales police helicopter near-miss
summary: A South Wales Police helicopter crew reported taking evasive action from a saucer-like object near MOD St Athan and pursued it towards the Bristol Channel. Nothing was seen on radar and no explanation was given.

title: Souther Fell spectral army
summary: On Midsummer evening 1745, 26 witnesses saw troops and carriages march along the ridge for hours; no tracks were found next day. Mirage explanations have been offered.

title: Spacesuit pranks confessed (Round Table hoax)
place: Haven Fort Hotel and Ripperston, Pembrokeshire
summary: Milford Haven Round Table member Glyn Edwards said in 1996 that he had roamed the area in a silver suit in 1977; Hilary Evans reported that two Round Table members using refinery asbestos/fire suits were behind the 'spacemen' at the Haven Fort and Ripperston. An RAF Police 'discreet enquiry' requested by the MoD in June 1977 concluded a practical joker could explain some events, though not the craft reports.

title: Spicers see creature cross road, Loch Ness
summary: George Spicer and his wife reported a long-necked animal crossing the road ahead of their car near the loch. Later researchers argued the account was coloured by the dinosaur scene in King Kong.

title: Spring-heeled Jack in Everton
summary: In 1904 crowds gathered on William Henry Street after rumours of a 'Spring-heel Jack'; missiles were thrown at a house until the tenants left, though police found nothing. A leaping figure was also claimed on St Francis Xavier's church roof in 1888.

title: Springhill House, Olivia
summary: Olivia Lenox-Conyngham is said to haunt the house and is described as one of Ireland's best-documented ghosts.

title: Sproatley orange balls
summary: A mother and daughter reported large orange balls, then a white ball with a shutter-like feature, a change in the sky's colour and a loud noise. A photo was claimed to show a figure.

title: St Columba and the River Ness beast
summary: Adomnan's life of St Columba, written about a century later, tells of the saint driving off a water beast that had attacked a man in the River Ness. Sceptics see it as a standard hagiographic motif.

title: St Margaret's Road medieval prisoner
place: St Hugh's College, St Margaret's Road, Oxford
summary: Eleanor Jourdain, later principal of St Hugh's, reported seeing a medieval prisoner being dragged along the road by a jeering crowd in period dress.

title: Stack Rocks: disc enters the rock and silver figures walk the islet
place: Stack Rocks, St Brides Bay, Pembrokeshire
summary: Pauline Coombs, her mother and children, driving the clifftop route by Broadmoor, reported a 40-50 ft disc that flew over the car and seemed to vanish into Stack Rocks through two sliding 'doors', reappear and return; later two silver figures were seen walking on the islet, one reportedly appearing to walk on the water. Rose Granville, who owned Stack Rocks, phoned to say she and her husband Hayden and daughter Francine had watched the same craft and figures through binoculars from the Haven Fort Hotel across the bay. The scene was drawn by artist Michael Buhler in 1978 ('Incident at Stack Rocks, Dyfed, Wales. 30-10-77', Government Art Collection); one retelling dates the event to March 1978.

title: Stainburn bypass triangle
summary: Over Christmas 2003 a triangular craft was reported over the Stainburn bypass heading towards the Lake District, among several West Cumbria sightings including a red object and an orange ball. No explanation was given.

title: Star-like object turns sharply over Denbigh
summary: A witness who said they had RAF experience first took the object for an aircraft about 8-10 miles away. It then changed direction at about 45 degrees and sped off, getting brighter as it went.

title: Starved maid of the Bear and Billet
place: Bear and Billet, Lower Bridge Street, Chester
summary: A maid who starved after being locked in a room haunts the stairs and shows herself only to men; mild poltergeist activity and screeches on the answerphone are also reported.

title: Steve Tyler's dome and transparent-suited figure near RAF Brawdy
place: Lane near Llethr / Hendre Bridge, Brawdy, Pembrokeshire
summary: Seventeen-year-old Steve Tyler reported an orange disc around 9pm, then a house-sized dome in a field that blocked out the lights of the Brawdy air base. A tall hairless figure in a transparent suit approached him; he said his punch passed through nothing and that his dog growled at him when he got home. Coordinates are for Llethr, Penycwm (approximate).

title: Stone-throwing ghost at farm between Bont and Tregaron
place: farm between Pontrhydfendigaid and Tregaron, Ceredigion
summary: John Jones of Pontrhydfendigaid, aged 95, told Ceredig Davies that a ghost haunting a farm between Pontrhydfendigaid and Tregaron threw stones, 'to the great discomfort of the family'.

title: Stone-throwing on Kirkland Street, St Helens
summary: For weeks stones, bricks and potatoes rained down on the street after dark, one knocking off a constable's helmet. Police believed a human culprit was responsible.

title: Striped sheepdog-sized cat, Denbigh
summary: Police logged a report of a silver-and-black animal about the size of a sheepdog with a broader dark stripe than a domestic cat would have.

title: Stronsay Beast carcass
summary: A huge decayed carcass, measured at 55 ft, washed ashore after a storm and was named as a new sea serpent species. Anatomists later concluded it was a decomposed basking shark.

title: Surrey Puma
summary: Sightings of a large wild cat began in 1964 and the press named it after Crondall and Munstead. Surrey Police reviewed 362 reported sightings between September 1964 and August 1966.

title: Suspected wolfman, Llyn Brianne
place: Llyn Brianne, upper Tywi valley, Carmarthenshire
summary: A suspected wolfman sighting at Llyn Brianne, reported first-hand to Bryn by someone he knows. Date, time and description still to add.

title: Talacre lighthouse keeper Raymond
place: Point of Ayr Lighthouse, Talacre, Flintshire
summary: A figure in old-fashioned clothing, believed to be the last keeper and nicknamed Raymond, is said to stand on the lantern balcony looking out to sea. A steel sculpture of him later stood there for a while.

title: Tall strangers in a silver car ask for Pauline Coombs
summary: The eldest Coombs boy, alone at home, reported two unusually tall people with bulging foreheads and large eyes arriving in a big silver car; he locked the door and they went to a neighbouring cottage (Caroline Klass) asking for Mrs Coombs, then left. One account says the car then turned up at the Haven Fort Hotel asking for Mrs Granville. Dated 6 June 1977 by Underwood via Jot101 and late June by Cambria Stories.

title: Talsarn smallholder blames big cat for sheep deaths
summary: A Talsarn pensioner lost three sheep over two days in July 2023, one eaten down to skin and bone, and reported it to police at Lampeter. She said she had seen a 'black leopard' at least five times over the years; a DEFRA post-mortem attributed the deaths to a dog.

title: Tawny cat and paw prints at Mynydd Isa
summary: At about 7pm a resident saw a brownish animal larger than a dog, with a long thin tail, run into a field. A Puma Watch volunteer later found several sets of large paw prints at the spot.

title: Teggie, the Llyn Tegid monster
summary: Since the 1920s people have reported a dinosaur-like creature in Wales's largest natural lake. A Japanese film crew with a mini-submarine found nothing in the 1990s, and a park warden puts the disturbances down to fish, gas bubbles or otters.

title: Tern Hill barracks lights
summary: Soldiers on fire picket filmed 13 lights over the barracks on a phone. A local landlord said they were Chinese lanterns from a wedding and the MoD accepted that.

title: Tharston 'scareship' airship
summary: During the 1909 'mystery airship' wave a cyclist reported a silent airship-like craft about 400 ft long; another was reported the same day at Wroxham. No explanation was established.

title: The Dodleston messages
summary: In 1984–85 teacher Ken Webster and his partner reported thrown objects and rearranged furniture at Meadow Cottage, then messages appearing on a borrowed BBC Micro. Most were signed 'Tomas Harden', who wrote in a form of 16th-century English and said he lived in the same house. Webster told the story in his book The Vertical Plane (1989). The case drew researchers from the Society for Psychical Research and is still argued over.

title: 'The Sarge' at the Woolton ambulance centre
summary: Ambulance crews blamed footsteps, broken windows and doors that unlocked themselves on 'the Sarge', a policeman killed when his patrol wagon hit a bollard.

title: The St Luke's abduction
place: Bold Place, behind St Luke's Church, Liverpool
summary: A six-year-old girl vanished from Bold Place behind the ruined church and was found holding the hand of a man in Victorian dress; she said an old woman in a shawl had led her inside. Researched by Tom Slemen.

title: The 'Surgeon's Photograph' hoax
summary: Robert Kenneth Wilson's famous long-necked photo appeared in the Daily Mail in April 1934. In 1991 one of those involved admitted it showed a toy submarine fitted with a model head and neck.

title: The Thing of Delamere
summary: Locals reported a dog-like animal about 60cm tall with a fox-like tail but an Alsatian look roaming the forest.

title: The Wash rotating object
summary: A police officer reported a rotating object that was also picked up on air traffic radar. The radar return was put down to St Botolph's Church in Boston and the visual sighting to a celestial object.

title: Thornton Heath Poltergeist
summary: Nandor Fodor investigated disturbances around Mrs Forbes in 1938 and concluded they were psychological in origin and partly fraudulent.

title: Tiger-sized black cat at Penmachno
summary: A caller told police they had seen a massive black puma-like cat in a field opposite a house. The police log describes it as tiger-sized, and officers investigated.

title: Tim Dinsdale's hump film, Loch Ness
summary: Aeronautical engineer Tim Dinsdale filmed a dark hump leaving a wake; a 1966 RAF analysis called it probably animate, but later work suggests a boat in poor light.

title: Tiny grey figure photographed, Balker Drive
summary: A woman testing a new phone camera later found one shot appeared to show a tiny grey alien-like figure walking along the road.

title: Tivoli Buckley glass thrown and CCTV figure
place: The Tivoli, Brunswick Road, Buckley, Flintshire
summary: The manager says a glass was thrown at him in an empty upstairs room. He and about six colleagues saw a figure hanging from a ceiling on the CCTV monitor that was gone when they checked. Staff blame a projectionist who died in a 1940s fire, and Most Haunted filmed there.

title: Alan Godfrey abduction
summary: A police officer saw a domed object over the road and lost time. Later hypnosis sessions described an abduction.

title: Trick-or-treating monk at Chester Cathedral
summary: A grey monk heard speaking old English was seen several times in the 1970s. On Halloween 2003 children offered him their sweet bag and he is said to have eaten the contents, wrappers and all.

title: Tusked creature in Antrim Bay, Lough Neagh
place: Antrim Bay, Lough Neagh, Co. Antrim
summary: A fisherman described an animal with a bull-sized head, walrus-like tusks and a large back fin swimming towards him before diving. A 1958 student 'monster' on the lough was a deliberate Rag Week hoax.

title: Twin-humped serpent, Loch Garry
summary: Two Australian visitors near the Glen Garry viewpoint saw a twin-humped serpent-like shape about 100 m offshore for around ten seconds.

title: Twin sightings over Caernarfon and Amlwch
summary: Within five minutes of each other, a red-and-green star-like object was seen over Caernarfon and a large blue glowing object that turned green, broke up and left smoke was seen over Amlwch. Both appear in the government's 2001 UFO report.

title: Two cars see long-tailed cat near Llanfechell
summary: A holidaymaker in one car saw a Labrador-sized black cat with a very long, thick tail in a roadside field. A friend in the car behind independently reported seeing it at the same spot.

title: Tywyn orange-to-white light
summary: A large bright orange light turned white and then vanished quickly without any sound. No explanation was given.

title: Vanishing figures on the Bridge of Sighs
place: Bridge of Sighs, Northgate Street, Chester
summary: In the late 1990s a cyclist looked up at the bridge and saw two or three people in old-fashioned clothes who then vanished. Condemned prisoners once crossed it to chapel.

title: Vanishing passenger on Halsall Moss
summary: In early 1965 a driver on the Southport-Ormskirk road saw an elderly man in a flat cap sitting in the back of his Mini, who had gone when he leapt out. Years later another man described the same thing at the same bridge.

title: Victorian miners' ghosts at Llywernog / Silver Mountain
place: Silver Mountain Experience (Llywernog mine), Ponterwyd, Ceredigion
summary: The former silver-lead mine is said to be haunted by the ghosts of former miners, with knocking sounds reported during underground tours. Paranormal investigations are now run there.

title: Walton Hall, Warrington
summary: Children's crying and laughter are heard on the stairs, a ghost girl is said to push visitors and Lady Daresbury is said to haunt her rooms.

title: The Warminster Thing
summary: Strange sounds and lights over the town drew sky-watchers to Cradle Hill for years.

title: Weedon Bec dumbbell lights and lost time
summary: Elsie Oakensen reported dumbbell-shaped lights above the road, her car cutting out, and about 15 minutes she could not account for. No explanation was given.

title: West Freugh radar object
place: RAF West Freugh, Dumfries and Galloway
summary: Radar at West Freugh tracked a large stationary target at about 50,000 ft that then climbed sharply and turned at speed. No explanation was published.

title: West Kilbride green saucer
summary: A member of the public reported a fluorescent green saucer appearing to harass an aircraft near Prestwick. No explanation was given.

title: White lady near Wylfa
summary: A woman in white is said to haunt the area around the Wylfa nuclear power station on Anglesey's north coast.

title: White Lady of Charles Fort
summary: A bride said to have died after her husband's killing on their wedding night haunts the walls; in 1922 a medical officer reported being pushed downstairs by a robed young woman.

title: White Lady of Prestatyn promenade
place: Prestatyn seafront near the Nova, Denbighshire
summary: A woman in a white dress is said to walk alone along the promenade and coast path between Prestatyn and Rhyl. Legend says she drowned herself in the sea.

title: White lady rising into the trees, Delamere
place: Delamere Forest near Delamere Station, Delamere
summary: Two walkers heading for Frodsham met a white lady who stared at them for minutes and then floated up into the trees.

title: White sphere drifts over Holyhead
summary: At 2.30pm a round, bright white object hovered and then moved slowly and silently from south-west to north-east near Holyhead.

title: Whitehaven golf course light
summary: Six people at the clubhouse saw a silent round light several feet across cross the sky, puff smoke, accelerate and drop onto the course. Searches found nothing.

title: Wicklow Gaol
summary: The gaol, used from 1702 to 1924, is said to be haunted by inmates who died there, many during the Famine.

title: Widnes black sphere with antenna
summary: A 17-year-old saw a black spherical craft with an antenna fly overhead. Ufologist Jenny Randles speculated it could have been a lost Merseyside Police drone.

title: William Batt, Oakwell Hall
summary: In December 1684 William Batt was reportedly seen arriving home at dusk and left a bloody footprint, on the day he was killed in London.

title: Wilmslow red light (crane)
summary: A caller reported a stationary red light to the east watched for 20 minutes after midnight. Cheshire Police established it was a light on a crane.

title: Wincolmlee police patrol UFO
summary: Two police officers on patrol reported watching an unidentified object pass over the city. No explanation was recorded.

title: Witch Peggy of Cilycwm and uncontrollable spirits
summary: A former butler at Blaennos told Ceredig Davies that an old witch at Cilycwm named Peggy struggled to control the spirits in her house. She sometimes had to stand in a protective circle in a field with a whip in her hand.

title: Woolton Hall stair ghost
place: Woolton Hall, Speke Road, Woolton, Liverpool
summary: Investigators report unease and a growl attributed to a Freemason's spirit, and a pregnant woman who lost her baby in a fall is said to walk the stairs.

title: Large black figure
place: Clyde Walkway behind Bothwell Castle, near Glasgow
summary: Walking his dogs on a Sunday afternoon, a man faced a featureless 7ft all-black figure clenching its fists in a clearing; his friends arrived and it vanished, with the dogs frozen in place.

title: Lights in the sky
place: Hunmanby Road just past the old Dotterel pub, Reighton
summary: A father and his daughter saw around six star-like lights moving oddly and shifting colour, and his partner filmed them on returning home.

title: Lights in the sky
place: Woodland path beside the Nugent estate and Anne Street, Portaferry
summary: A walker saw a grapefruit-sized white-blue light weave playfully through bare branches; years later he saw a pillow-sized rugby-ball light glide low over the estate field.

title: Ghost haunting campers
place: Ballyherly fishing lake on the Nugent estate, Portaferry
summary: Two friends camping by the lake saw an invisible something press bulges into their tent wall and roof that slid towards the open flap, yet nothing was outside in the moonlit field.

title: Balls of light
summary: During a storm with silent sheet lightning, a couple in a campervan saw two orange-red balls of light hover about 20ft away for a few seconds, then a third; the next night Tim reports further oddities at the cliff viewpoint.

title: Tic-tac shaped object
place: Back garden in Yatton, North Somerset
summary: Around 2007 a woman watched a shiny silver tic-tac shaped object hover beside a cloud for about half a minute, feeling observed, before it darted sideways behind the cloud.

title: Ghostly festivities
place: Servants' quarters behind the mansion on the Nugent estate, Portaferry, County Down
summary: In 1982 six family members lying in bed heard music, laughter and many conversations, like a grand ball, from the empty Georgian mansion next door before it faded to silence.

title: Small beings and an implant
place: Bedroom of a home in West Yorkshire
summary: A woman who believed she was newly pregnant woke to three 3ft beings in her doorway telepathically telling her not to wake; weeks later she found a tiny chip-like object in an itchy lump on her wrist.

title: Doppelgänger encounter
summary: Driving to work around 1999, a man passed an identical red car with his number plate and mismatched door, and its driver was himself, gasping back at him.

title: Lights and an object in the sky
place: Road from Wadworth to Tickhill, South Yorkshire
summary: Two young women driving home late repeatedly saw glowing white lights pace their car through the fields from Wadworth to Tickhill all summer; the witness and her father later saw an unknown craft near Stainton.

title: Cryptid
place: Track down to Man Sands near Brixham, Devon
summary: In 1989 two friends walking to their tent at dusk heard heavy hooves before a 4.5ft creature with huge eyes dropped onto the track, growled and advanced when gravel was thrown at it.

title: Strange feline
place: Woodland on the old Loganlea pit bing, Addiewell, West Lothian
summary: Out running, a man saw a dark grey or black cat the size of a Labrador break cover onto the path, stare at him for a few seconds and vanish into the undergrowth.

title: Silver ball in the sky
summary: In 1968 a six-year-old and her brothers watched a satin-sheened metallic sphere that seemed to follow her movements through the tree branches before rising silently and flying off.

title: Disc in the sky
place: Shaw near Rochdale, looking towards Saddleworth
summary: A couple watched a shiny silver ball sit in a clear sky, then drop, stop and dart left and right with instant starts before departing.

title: Disc in the sky
place: Blue Bank on the A169, near RAF Fylingdales
summary: Early one morning a resident photographed a bright globular disc moving around near the sun before it travelled east towards the coast and disappeared.

title: Translucent rectangle
place: North Park entrance at Cumberland Street, Darlington
summary: Two friends hiding from a feeling of being followed watched a van-sized translucent dark rectangle, like television static, glide between trees, fold up like a curtain and drift on while a street lamp dimmed.

title: Large black cryptid
place: Back garden in Hayes, west London
summary: Around 2001 two boys woke to see a giant black wolf-like creature with a long snout, snarling teeth and pointed ears stroll across the lit garden and leap the fence.

title: Black triangle that vanished
place: Drypool, east Hull, looking towards the Humber mouth
summary: Woken by a hovering search-and-rescue helicopter, a man saw a solid black triangle with white corner lights hanging still near it; when the searchlight found it the triangle vanished.

title: Orange lights in the sky
summary: In January 1967 a woman driving home saw two bright orange spheres towards Flamborough, followed them to Bempton and watched for twenty minutes until they descended into the sea about a mile out.

title: Lights in the sky
place: Frimley, above the Golden Lake nature reserve, Surrey
summary: Arriving home in the early hours, a man filmed large bright white lights that slowly descended, blinked out and reappeared, at one point forming a triangle.

title: Cryptid grunting
place: Roman Camp National Trust woodland, West Runton, Norfolk
summary: Two ex-servicemen wild camping heard pig-like grunting circle them; later something silently shoved the witness's tarp and brushed along his hammock, leaving him with unexplained fear.

title: Shadow figure
place: Roman-era field on the Yorkshire Wolds
summary: Metal detecting on a Roman site, a couple saw a distorted, heat-haze humanoid figure run past just as a silver coin was handed over; later visits brought nausea, roaring sounds and torch failures.

title: UFO update (follow-up to report 215)
place: Field between Danes Dyke and Wold Farm, near Bempton
summary: An expanded account of report 215: walking with Paul Sinclair and his grandson, the witness describes a decaying smell Paul noticed, then the flat object gliding across the field and apparently vanishing into the ground where they had crossed the fence.

title: Ghostly apparition
place: Tea rooms on Frimley High Street, Surrey
summary: During a ghost investigation at reputedly haunted tea rooms, an investigator heard footsteps upstairs and later found what looks like a reaching hand in one low-light photo.

title: Classic disc-shaped UFO
place: Farm track through wheat off New Street, Deddington, Oxfordshire
summary: In July 1974 six children saw a 15ft silver disc with a dark window band glide towards them just above a wheat field with a low hum before it shot up into the sky.

title: Giant unworldly figure
place: Field gateway on the road from Tuxford towards Nottingham
summary: In 1985 three scooter riders passing through low mist at night saw a tall scarecrow-like figure with a grey grimacing face and hollow dark eyes in old gamekeeper clothing standing at a field gate.

title: Yellow eyes
place: Clifftop path just past Staple Newk, towards RSPB Bempton
summary: On a moonlit cliff walk, a man shone his torch over the edge and saw a pair of large round yellow eyes set unusually wide apart staring up from the cliff face before the unseen creature turned away.

title: Cryptid
place: Woods and farmland behind Boothferry Road, Hessle
summary: A night-time poacher in the late 1980s felt something large and unseen watching him in eerily silent woods after hearing a heavy branch snap, and never went out at night again.

title: Bright light in the sky
place: Above St Catherine's Lighthouse, Niton, Isle of Wight
summary: Walking towards the lighthouse at dusk, a man saw a bright white light hanging just above it which arced down and then shot out to sea at great speed.

title: Cryptid running across a field
place: Field beside the A165 between the Dotterel roundabout, Reighton and Muston
summary: Driving back to Scarborough, a couple saw a huge top-heavy creature run across a stubble field with an odd gorilla-like gait on all fours.

title: Bright light in the sky
place: Model Farm fishing lake near Bewholme, between Hornsea and Skipsea
summary: At night a farmer saw a large bright light low over his fields; at dawn he photographed a hole punched through the clouds, shaped like an upturned wizard's hat, in the same spot.

title: Shadowy forms
summary: After moving into a new flat, a woman heard footsteps creep up the hall and turned to see a black shape slip round a corner while her husband was in the kitchen; other odd incidents followed.

title: Big cat

summary: On a windy night, a holidaymaker heard huge rhythmic wingbeats approach and seemingly settle outside his window, followed by shrieking; he says staff were also witnesses.

title: Large black cat
place: Fields beside the railway just south of Knebworth
summary: From an early train a commuter saw a large black cat-like animal running up a field towards woods; a big cat sanctuary was later found to lie beyond those woods.

title: Lights in the sky
place: Retreat centre in County Wexford, Ireland
summary: Stargazing from a window, a woman filmed flashing lights over the sea which repeatedly blinked out abruptly, unlike aircraft.

title: Light in the sky
place: B1253 just past the Octon roundabout, looking towards Stamford Bridge
summary: Driving home late, a man saw a bright vertical elliptical light appear high in the sky towards Stamford Bridge and fade out within seconds.

summary: A man saw and filmed a silent row of six lights alternating green and red that rose and drifted slowly away south.

title: Lights in the sky

title: Black figure
summary: A man on restricted army ground photographed a distant brown upright figure which he believes was a bigfoot.

title: Black figure
place: Box bedroom of a house in Sleaford, Lincolnshire
summary: A man woke on his back to a solid jet-black cloaked figure floating just above him; he rolled out and felt it pressing after him as he reached the light switch, where it vanished.

title: Cigar-shaped object
place: Over the English Channel, seen from an airliner
summary: A passenger flying from Istanbul watched a small cigar-shaped object drift very slowly for about fifteen minutes while private jets passed it quickly.

title: Disappearing figure
place: Hill Farm onshore oil site between Winchester and Stockbridge
summary: A lone night-shift oil worker saw a faceless figure, black below and red above, run across the lit site and vanish mid-leap; police called afterwards found nothing.

title: Black apparition
place: Cobden Close, Hednesford, on the edge of Cannock Chase
summary: Two children saw a 6 to 7ft black hooded figure with glowing red eyes by the fridge; in the bedroom where they hid the locked door unlocked, the air turned cold and the figure stood over them before rising to the loft.

title: Large black cat
place: Track to a poultry farm just west of Kilnwick, East Yorkshire
summary: A farm worker looking down a stone track saw a long, athletic black cat like a puma with a long curled tail.

title: Object in the sky
place: Garden on the outskirts of Chesterfield
summary: Through powerful binoculars a man watched a white ball with a gold light circling it travel along an aircraft contrail, then a second shape-shifting object follow the same path, which he photographed over about 35 minutes.

title: Dogman
place: Industrial site at Rawcliffe Bridge, north of Crowle Moors
summary: Night-shift workers in a fenced smoking area repeatedly felt watched and heard heavy movement and two distinct footsteps in the treeline by the railway, which the witness believes was a dogman.

title: Object in the sky
place: Broadgate near Monks Road, below Lincoln Cathedral
summary: A community nurse stuck at traffic lights watched a white oblong craft, a little smaller than a bus, cross slowly above the cathedral from east to west.

title: Light in the sky
place: Back of a fast-food shop in Whitehaven
summary: Three workers on a cigarette break saw a marble-like ball of light bobbing up and down in the sky, photographed and briefly filmed it, before it disappeared.

summary: Walking his dog, a man photographed a black object moving with a juddery yet effortless glide that looped and climbed into cloud; he half suspects a hang glider.

title: Large oval light in the sky

title: Lights in the sky

summary: A regular walker saw three silent orange balls in a triangle drift south over the lake, each outer light darting away and back to the formation in turn.

summary: A taxi driver and his passenger saw three silent round objects each with a steady red glow follow the River Tees out to sea before splitting up over Teesport.

title: Dogman

title: UFO in the sky and landing

title: Yellow light in the sky

summary: A retired police officer recalls shadowy featureless figures floating out of his bedroom wall as a small child; his parents later revealed a large white owl had repeatedly sat at his window. He goes on to describe later UFO experiences.

summary: A driver saw a steady warm-yellow light descend slowly in the sky above the hills, then shrink and wink out; he acknowledges a flare from RAF Boulmer is possible.

title: Three UFOs
place: Junction of Grindale Lane, Bridlington, looking over the Priory
summary: A driver pulling out of Grindale Lane saw three white cigar-shaped craft with possible portholes hanging over the Priory area; they were gone after a glance in his mirror.

summary: While trying to photograph the aurora a mother saw a sudden chain of very bright orange lights flare far out over the sea and captured them in long-exposure photos.

title: Triangle in the sky

summary: Paul Sinclair filmed three bright star-like lights moving away silently over the sea as if one huge triangular object; a contact separately saw a similar formation from the A69 the next morning.

summary: A rural postman in about 1998 watched a large black cat, at first mistaken for a cow because of its size, saunter across a field towards the tree line.

summary: A woman driving home at dusk saw a jet-black animal shaped like a small bear but with a long tail bound across the road from the bikers' cafe and into a hedge gap.

title: Lights in the sky

title: White light in the sky

summary: A family account: parents driving over the moors north of Bolton in the 1970s saw a shiny spinning disc hover then race off, and years later a brother saw a glowing blue-purple rectangle in the same area; other family ghost experiences are also mentioned.

summary: Driving home from Bridlington, a man saw a hooded girl with two small children by the road; the girl dashed across in front of the car ahead and vanished into a solid hedge, the children were gone, and neither his wife nor the other driver reacted.

title: Object in the night sky

summary: At 2:30am a lone photographer in Bempton shot a purplish-pink light that blinked in and out with a pink cloud-like effect around it, later spotting a second small light in the frame.

title: Silver disc in the sky

summary: Two women leaving the M6 in summer 1989 saw a round, shiny metallic object high up that turned on edge and disappeared; the local paper reported a wok-like UFO nearby that week.

title: Orange light in the sky
place: View from Norton Canes High School towards Heath Hayes, Staffordshire
summary: In 1982/83 a pupil gazing out of a classroom window saw a large flat orange ball cross between two spoil heaps, appearing to bounce in mid-air.

title: Orange light in the sky

summary: Two dog walkers on Lyth Hill saw a bright stationary orange light appear over Wenlock Edge, hold for about thirty seconds and then dim away as if on a dimmer switch.

summary: At a rally bonfire around 2am a man watched a pair of orange satellite-like lights cross the sky and then stop dead overhead as a genuine satellite passed them; they stayed fixed for around fifteen minutes before vanishing.

summary: Using binoculars, a man, his son and his wife watched a stationary metallic ball for nearly an hour; the man then saw it slowly rotate to reveal a cigar or cylinder shape before it was lost.

title: White rectangle in the sky

title: Triangle and light in the sky

title: Lights in the sky
summary: A late-night observer saw a white light fade in and out, flash, and zip sideways at an angle before vanishing.

title: Objects in the sky

title: Lights in the sky

title: Orange light in the sky

summary: A family saw a pure white triangle move jerkily over a hilltop and glide down and back up the slope without turning.

summary: Four witnesses in two households saw large silent glowing white balls of light hang and then move off over Bridlington after midnight.
